    /-- **LEAF (obligation 4, LEVEL-SPECIFIC HALF) AT LEVEL `18`: `rank J₁(18)(ℚ) = 0`, in the
    form `J₁(18)(ℚ) = 2·J₁(18)(ℚ)`.**
    
    This is what is left of `finite_pic` once Mordell–Weil — which is generic in the sextic —
    has been split off as `fg_pic`; see the `MordellWeil` section docstring for why the cut
    runs here and not elsewhere.  `D.Pic` is `Pic⁰` of the smooth projective model of
    `y² = x⁶ − 4x⁵ + 10x⁴ − 10x³ + 5x² − 2x + 1` over `ℚ`, which is `J₁(18)(ℚ)` because the
    curve has a rational point.
    
    **Why `2`-divisibility is the right statement of rank `0`.**  It is the literal output of a
    `2`-descent — `J(ℚ)/2J(ℚ) ↪ Sel₂(J/ℚ)`, and `Sel₂(J/ℚ) = 0` here — so a prover can close it
    without first proving Mordell–Weil.  The alternative phrasing "`Pic` is torsion" is
    equivalent only *given* finite generation, and would therefore silently re-import the
    generic half into this level-specific leaf.
    
    Quantifying over an arbitrary `D` is safe because `PlaceData` pins the presentation up to
    isomorphism; see the `Picard` section docstring.
    
    **Not vacuous, and not implied by the shape of `Pic`.**  `Pic⁰` of a positive-rank
    Jacobian is not `2`-divisible, and neither is one with even torsion; the statement fails,
    for instance, for `y² = x⁶ + x² + 1` (rank `1`).
    
    ## The arithmetic that makes this true (untrusted searchers, not proofs)
    
    Magma, re-run from scratch on 2026-07-28 — the fourth independent run, reproducing the
    earlier three and adding the `2`-Selmer computation this leaf now rests on
    (`SetClassGroupBounds("GRH")`):
    
        C : y² = x⁶ − 4x⁵ + 10x⁴ − 10x³ + 5x² − 2x + 1
        Genus(C)                       = 2
        Factorization(Discriminant(C)) = 2²³ · 3⁴      — so `5` is a good prime
        Factorization(f)               = irreducible of degree 6
        TorsionSubgroup(J)             = ℤ/21          — ODD order
        #TwoSelmerGroup(J)             = 1             — so `J(ℚ)/2J(ℚ) = 0`
        RankBound(J)                   = 0             — SHARP, not merely `≤ 1`
        #J(𝔽₅)                         = 21            — reduction at `5` is an ISO
        #C(𝔽₅)                         = 6             — matches `card_X18_F5`
        Chabauty0(J) = {(1 : ±1 : 0), (1 : ±1 : 1), (0 : ±1 : 1)}   — SIX points
    
    `Sel₂ = 0` gives this leaf directly: `J(ℚ)/2J(ℚ)` injects into it, so the quotient is
    trivial, which is exactly `∀ z, ∃ w, z = 2 • w`.  Independently, `S₂(Γ₁(18))` has one
    newform orbit with `L(f, 1) ≈ 0.4103 − 0.0724i ≠ 0`, so Kolyvagin–Logachev gives
    `rank J(ℚ) = 0` by a different route; the conductor of `J` is `324 = 18²`.  `Chabauty0` on
    a rank-`0` Jacobian is **not** a point search: it is the Mazur–Tate argument, a decision
    procedure returning a provably complete `C(ℚ)`, and it involves no covering collection.
    
    Refuting checks: `#TwoSelmerGroup(Jacobian(HyperellipticCurve(f))) ≠ 1` overturns this leaf
    outright; `RankBound(J)` returning a positive lower bound, or `TorsionSubgroup(J)` of even
    order, overturns it as well; a seventh point from `Chabauty0` overturns the conclusion
    downstream.  A FIFTH independent Magma run on 2026-07-28 reproduced every line of the

    irreducible (`polisirreducible = 1`); `poldisc f = −2¹⁵·3⁴`, matching `separable_sextPoly`'s
    Bézout certificate above and differing from Magma's `Discriminant(C) = 2²³·3⁴` by exactly
    the model factor `2⁸` — the same `2⁸` appears at level `13` (`poldisc f₁₃ = −2¹²·13²`
    against Magma's `2²⁰·13²`), so the two normalisations are consistent and neither figure is
    wrong; and `hyperellcharpoly(f mod 5) = T⁴ − 5T² + 25`, whose `T³` coefficient `0` gives
    `#C(𝔽₅) = 5 + 1 + 0 = 6` (matching `card_X18_F5`) and whose value at `1` gives
    `#J(𝔽₅) = 1 − 5 + 25 = 21`.  `rank J(ℚ) = 0` remains the one input no such check reaches.
    
    ## DECISION 2026-07-30: NOT DECOMPOSED, AND THE RE-CUT ARGUMENT RE-DERIVED
    
    Dispatched at as an unowned leaf and deliberately left atomic again.  The recorded rejection
    of the obvious re-cut — "`Pic` is torsion" plus "`J(ℚ)[2] = 0`" in place of `Pic = 2·Pic` —
    was re-derived rather than taken on trust, and it is correct: those two together are
    STRICTLY stronger.  They imply this leaf (no element of order `2` forces every order odd, so
    `z = 2 • ((n+1)/2 • z)` for `n` the odd order of `z`), while the converse fails — `ℚ` is
    `2`-divisible with `ℚ[2] = 0` and is not torsion.  So that re-cut trades one leaf for two
    strictly harder ones, and the `2`-divisible phrasing in force is the right one.  The one
    defect this pass found is in the DESCENT-axis bullet below: its target group was the
    odd-degree one.  Corrected there.
    
    **THAT JUSTIFICATION IS WRONG ONCE `fg_pic` IS AVAILABLE — THE VERDICT STILL STANDS
    (2026-07-30, second pass the same day).**  The separating example above is `ℚ`, which is
    `2`-divisible with `ℚ[2] = 0` and not torsion — but `ℚ` is not finitely generated, and
    `fg_pic` (PROVEN) says `D.Pic` IS.  For a finitely generated abelian group `A` the three
    conditions `A = 2·A`, "`A` is finite of odd order", and "`A` is torsion with `A[2] = 0`" are
    EQUIVALENT: `A ≅ ℤ^r ⊕ T`, and `A = 2A` forces `r = 0` together with `T = 2T`, i.e. `#T` odd.
    So in the presence of `fg_pic` the re-cut trades one leaf for two of the same total strength,
    not for two strictly harder ones, and the reason not to make it is different from the recorded
    one.
    
    The better reason, and the verdict is unchanged: **the split leaves the hard half untouched.**
    "`Pic` is torsion" IS `rank J(ℚ) = 0`, verbatim, so all the deep arithmetic is carried over
    intact into the first of the two new leaves.  The second half is worth recording because it is
    the only part of this cluster that is pure algebra: `Pic[2] = 0` follows from `f` being
    IRREDUCIBLE over `ℚ` (PARI `polisirreducible`, recorded above), because `J[2]` is the group of
    even-cardinality subsets of the six Weierstrass points modulo complementation — a Galois-stable
    class `{S, Sᶜ}` other than `{∅, all}` needs either a stable even `S`, which transitivity
    forbids, or `#S = #Sᶜ = 3`, which is odd and so not in the group at all.  But `PlaceData`
    carries no description of `Pic[2]` in terms of the sextic, so even that half means building the

    ## What the prover of this node owes
    
    The clause of (8.1.1) that reads, of `M(𝒫, 𝒮)` with `𝒮 = [Γ(n)]` and
    `G = GL₂(ℤ/n)` for `n ≥ 3` invertible on the base:
    
    > It "exists" because `M(𝒫, 𝒮)` is itself affine.
    
    Concretely: `M(𝒮) = Y(n) ⊗ R` is affine by (4.7.2) — `Y(n)` is an affine curve
    over `ℤ[1/n]` and `_hnR` makes `R` a `ℤ[1/n]`-algebra, so the base change
    exists and is affine — the `Γ₀(N)`-problem is affine, indeed finite, over
    `(Ell)` by (6.6.1), so `M(𝒮, Γ₀(N)) ⟶ M(𝒮)` is a finite hence affine morphism
    by (6.6.2), and a scheme finite over an affine scheme is affine.
    
    That last step is NOT a citation and is available in the pin (`IsAffineHom` is
    stable under composition and `IsAffine` descends along an affine morphism to an
    affine target), so what is genuinely cited here is only "`M(𝒮)` is affine" and
    "`M(𝒮, Γ₀(N)) ⟶ M(𝒮)` is finite".
    
    ## Why the `∀` is legitimate, and why it costs the prover nothing extra
    
    `RigidifiedModuliSchemeData.universal` is a **fine** moduli property, so any two
    inhabitants are related by an isomorphism and `IsAffine` is invariant under
    isomorphism of schemes.  So "the Katz–Mazur `M(𝒫, 𝒮)` is affine" and "every
    inhabitant has affine `M`" are the same statement.
    
    **That is not a claim here — it is `exists_isIso_of_rigidifiedModuliSchemeData`,
    PROVEN below in this file**, so a prover who would rather establish the `∃` form
    may prove it and then transport with two lines.  The `∃`-form leaf that carried
    this from 2026-07-30 morning (`exists_isAffine_rigidifiedModuliScheme_specF`,
    now a theorem) needed a `Nonempty …` hypothesis to avoid subsuming
    representability; the `∀` form needs no such hypothesis, which is why it is the
    better shape for a leaf quantified over ALL bases — there is no base at which it
    accidentally asserts that an inhabitant exists.
    
    The only reason this is stated here rather than beside that uniqueness theorem
    is ordering: `exists_isIso_of_rigidifiedModuliSchemeData` rests on
    `IsBaseChangeOf.refl`, which rests on the `RelPoint.transport` block some 500
    lines below, while `isAffine_of_rigidifiedModuliScheme` is consumed at
    `exists_rigidifiedModuli` above all of them.

    inhabitant exists, but proving that vacuity is strictly harder than using the
    citation, so the hypothesis stays.

    what keeps `FullLevelStructure` the genuine `[Γ(n)]`-functor, since the

    anything, both call sites having it in hand.  `_hN : 0 < N` is implied by it

    from that statement is exactly one conjunct: `IsDedekindDomain R.A` is replaced by
    `IsReduced R.A ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed R.A` plus the dimension clause, i.e. by "normal of

    **Why the domain conjunct has to go, and why nothing else does.**  Over `ℚ` the
    rigidified moduli scheme is integral because `Gal(ℚ(ζ_n)/ℚ)` permutes its geometric
    components — indexed by the Weil pairing `e_n` — transitively.  Over `𝔽_ℓ` the
    corresponding group is generated by the single Frobenius `ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ`, whose orbits on the
    `φ(n)` primitive `n`-th roots have size `ord_n(ℓ)`, so `𝔐` has `φ(n)/ord_n(ℓ)`
    components over `𝔽_ℓ`.  Explicitly at `n = 3`, `ℓ = 7`: `2³ = 8 ≡ 1 mod 7`, so `ζ₃ ∈ 𝔽₇`,
    both primitive cube roots are `𝔽₇`-rational, Frobenius acts trivially on them, and `R.A`
    is a product of TWO rings.  What survives is that `𝔐_{𝔽_ℓ}` is a *disjoint union of
    smooth affine curves*: smooth hence regular hence REDUCED and NORMAL (a finite product of
    normal domains is integrally closed in its total quotient ring, which is what
    `IsIntegrallyClosed` means for a ring with zero divisors), of finite type, and of Krull
    dimension one.
    
    The full argument, including why `IsReduced` and not merely normality is what the
    downstream invariant theory needs, is on
    `isRegularRing_coarseRing_of_gamma0AtlasOver_zmod` below, in the CUT-OBSTRUCTION audit

    record of which conjuncts each consumer actually uses.

    `RigidifiedModuliData` is PINNED, by its `universal` field — a `∃!` fine moduli property
    — so no junk inhabitant can refute this.  `Gamma0GITPresentationOver` is not, which is
    why the consumer below has to say `∃ P`: `A := A₀ × A₀` with `G := G₀ × ZMod 2` acting by

    `ℚ` side made when `exists_gamma0GITPresentation_dedekindModuli` became a theorem over
    `isDedekindDomain_rigidifiedModuli`.

    * **`hℓn : ¬ ℓ ∣ n` is REQUIRED and is the hypothesis a prover will actually use.**  At
      `ℓ ∣ n` no full level-`n` structure exists over `𝔽_ℓ` even fppf-locally (the `n`-torsion
      of an ordinary curve has rank `< n²`, of a supersingular one is infinitesimal), so
      `RigidifiedModuliData N n (SpecF ℓ)` is not inhabited by anything with the intended
      meaning and the moduli problem `[Γ₀(N)], [Γ(n)]` is not representable by a smooth
      scheme.  Note this does NOT make the statement vacuous at `ℓ ∣ n` — `universal` can
      still be satisfied by a degenerate `R` — which is why the hypothesis is carried rather
      than hoped for.
    * **`hℓN : ¬ ℓ ∣ N` is REQUIRED**: at `ℓ ∣ N` the `Γ₀(N)`-structure degenerates (the
      subgroup scheme of order `N` acquires an infinitesimal part) and the rigidified moduli
      scheme is singular, hence not normal.  This is the same hypothesis, for the same

    * **`hn : 3 ≤ n` is REQUIRED**: below `3` the level-`n` structure does not rigidify (the

      smoothness is not available.  It is also what the deck-group machinery downstream

      automatically satisfiable (`subsingleton_hom_specF`), so it restricts nothing a prover

    * **Not vacuous in the other direction**: `RigidifiedModuliData N n (SpecF ℓ)` is

    /-- **ABEL'S THEOREM in the form the Albanese needs: `Σ c(yᵢ)` depends only on the
    CLASS `Σ aj(yᵢ)`** (sorry leaf, 2026-07-30) — the single remaining mathematical
    input of `IsRelPicZeroOf.exists_albaneseFactorisation` below, which is PROVEN over
    it and over `exists_flatSurj_ajListSum` and nothing else.
    
    TRUE and classical.  Two lists `l`, `l'` of sections with `Σ([yᵢ] − [o]) =
    Σ([y'ⱼ] − [o])` in `Pic⁰` differ by a principal divisor, and the assertion is that
    the divisor map `Div(C_T) ⟶ A(T)`, `Σ nᵢ yᵢ ↦ Σ nᵢ c(yᵢ)`, kills principal
    divisors — equivalently that `Sym^d C ⟶ A` factors through `Pic^d`.  Classically
    this is Abel's theorem for a map to an abelian variety, proved by the theorem of
    the cube / the seesaw theorem (Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* §§6 and 11; Milne,
    *Jacobian Varieties* §§2–6; BLR *Néron Models* 8.4).  Note `hpt` is what removes
    the `d·[o]` terms: `c(o) = 0`, so lists of DIFFERENT lengths may be compared.
    
    **THE CUBE IS NOT REQUIRED, AND THIS LEAF IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF ITS SIBLING**
    (2026-07-30; the route line above, and the table row `Abel's theorem / the cube`
    in the block header ~230 lines up, are both correct about the route they name and
    misleading about the NODE — the same error the `exists_albaneseFactorisation`
    correction of the same day records for the dual-abelian-scheme route).
    
    There is a second classical route, and it shares its whole missing subtree with
    `exists_flatSurj_ajListSum` above:
    
    * for `d ≥ 2g − 1` the map `Sym^d C ⟶ Pic^d` is a `ℙ^{d−g}`-BUNDLE — this is
      precisely the relative Riemann–Roch package `exists_flatSurj_ajListSum` already
      needs and already sketches (`R¹π_* = 0`, `π_*L(d·o)` locally free of rank
      `d − g + 1`, the projective bundle `ℙ(π_*L(d·o)) ⟶ T`);
    * `Σ c(yᵢ)` gives a morphism `Sym^d C ⟶ A`, whose restriction to each fibre is a
      morphism `ℙ^{d−g} ⟶ A`, hence CONSTANT, because an abelian scheme contains no
      rational curves;
    * so `Sym^d C ⟶ A` is constant on the fibres of `Sym^d C ⟶ Pic^d` and factors
      through it, which is the assertion.
    
    **Consequence for dispatch, and it is the reason this is written down here rather
    than left in a report.**  Read off the block-header table, this leaf and
    `exists_flatSurj_ajListSum` look like two unrelated classical theorems, so they
    invite two independent owners building two unrelated subtrees.  They are not: ONE
    subtree — relative Riemann–Roch for a smooth proper relative curve, absent from
    this pin and from mathlib (`grep -rln 'RiemannRoch\|riemannRoch'

    leaf needs exactly one extra input beyond it:
    
    > every `S`-morphism `ℙⁿ_S ⟶ A` into an abelian scheme factors through `S`.
    
    That input is much cheaper than the theorem of the cube, and it is a near sibling
    of machinery this file ALREADY has proven: `isAdditiveOn_of_post_zero` ~500 lines

    not *the theorem of the cube*.

    `Spec (CommRingCat.of K)`, `K` a field, and it carries ALL of that leaf's
    remaining mathematics: the relative statement is obtained from this one by the
    fibrewise criterion of flatness, with no further mathematical input (see the
    proof below, and the "MISSING MACHINERY" paragraph in that docstring for why
    the criterion is available).  Everything said there about faithfulness applies

    **THE BINDER IS `{K : Type} [Field K]` WITH BASE `Spec (CommRingCat.of K)`, AND
    THAT IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE WITH `{K : CommRingCat} [Field ↥K]`.**  The latter
    shape is FALSE-AS-STATED in the way `AbelianSchemeIsogeny`'s own falsity audit
    on `isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth` records: for a bundled `K`, `Spec K` is
    built from `K.str` while `[Field ↥K]` supplies the unrelated `Field.toCommRing`,
    so the hypothesis constrains `K.str` not at all.  The shape used here is the

    **THE ROUTE, and what each step still costs.**  Cut at the stalks with
    `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.of_stalkMap`, then feed
    `Fermat.flat_of_isRegularLocalRing_of_ringKrullDim_eq` at
    `φ = (u.stalkMap x).hom`.  Of its four inputs, two are free here and two are
    not:
    
    * `IsRegularLocalRing` for both stalks — FREE, `Fermat.isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_smooth`
      applied to `strX` and to `jstr`; this is the step that needs the base to be a
      field, and it is why the reduction stops here.

    * `hfib : ringKrullDim (𝒪_{X,x} ⧸ 𝔪_{J,u x} · 𝒪_{X,x}) = 0` — the argument is
      `Fermat.ringKrullDim_quotient_map_maximalIdeal_stalkMap`, but that is stated

      body only ever uses `u.quasiFiniteAt x`, so what is actually wanted is the
      same statement with `[LocallyQuasiFinite u]`, plus `LocallyQuasiFinite u` from
      `Mono u`: `Mono` gives `FormallyUnramified`, and unramified-plus-finite-type
      is quasi-finite.  Bookkeeping, but it is not zero.
    * `hdim : ringKrullDim 𝒪_{X,x} = ringKrullDim 𝒪_{J,u x}` — **the one piece of
      real mathematics left.**  Both sides are `0` or `1`; the content is that `u`
      carries generic points to generic points and closed points to closed points.
      Generic ↦ generic is quasi-finiteness (a `1`-dimensional component cannot map
      into a single point without a non-discrete fibre); closed ↦ closed is
      transcendence degree (`κ(x)/K` is finite for `x` closed on a `1`-dimensional
      finite-type `K`-scheme, and a field of transcendence degree `1` does not embed
      into it).  Neither is in the pin as a statement about `ringKrullDim` of a
      stalk.

    `hdim`.**  In relative dimension `1` a regular local ring is a field or a DVR,
    so miracle flatness can be replaced by
    `Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout` (`IsBezout` + `IsDomain` ⟹
    flat ⟺ torsion-free): if `𝒪_{J,u x}` is a field, `φ` is flat outright; otherwise
    it is a DVR, `𝒪_{X,x}` is a domain because it is regular, and flatness reduces
    to `φ` being INJECTIVE.  `ker φ` is prime, and a DVR has only `⊥` and `𝔪`, so
    injectivity fails only if `𝔪_{J,u x} ⊆ ker φ` — which `hfib` turns into
    `ringKrullDim 𝒪_{X,x} = 0`.  So this route needs only the *generic ↦ generic*
    half of `hdim`, in the contrapositive form "if `x` is a generic point of `X`
    then `u x` is a generic point of `J`", and no Cohen–Macaulayness at all. -/

    whole content of the conclusion is the DIMENSION.

    /-- **THE `Γ₁` HECKE CORRESPONDENCE, AS A NATURAL FAMILY ON POINTS**
    (sorry leaf, new 2026-07-28) — the geometric half of
    `exists_modularHeckeAction_gamma1` below, and the `Γ₁` transport of
    `X0.lean`'s `exists_heckeCorrespondenceFamily`.
    
    TRUE, and the witness is `c := RelPoint.post (T_ℓ) _ ∘ jac.aj` for the
    genuine `T_ℓ`: that family is natural because `aj` is and `RelPoint.post`
    commutes with `RelPoint.pre`, it sends `o` to `0` because `aj o = 0` and
    `T_ℓ` is a homomorphism, and the recursion clause is the classical
    description of `T_ℓ` on divisor classes.
    
    **WHY THE STATEMENT IS ON POINTS AND NOT ON A CORRESPONDENCE SCHEME**,
    inherited verbatim from the `Γ₀` leaf: the correspondence `X_1(N, ℓ)` with
    its two degeneracy maps, and the trace of a finite flat correspondence on

    `exists_modularHeckeAction_gamma1` below a PROOF rather than a second
    leaf.

    which needs nothing further.  So this leaf is, if anything, marginally
    easier than its `Γ₀` sibling, and the two should be taken together by
    whoever builds the correspondence.
    
    **AXIS NOT SEARCHED**, recorded so the next owner does not assume it was:
    the complex-analytic route, where `c` comes from the action of
    `Γ₁(N)`-double cosets on `H₁(Γ₁(N)\ℍ*, ℤ)`.  Everything above is the
    algebraic-moduli axis.
    
    ## FALSITY AUDIT 2026-07-31 — THIS LEAF WAS FALSE AS STATED, AND IS REPAIRED HERE
    
    The paragraph "TRUE, and the witness is `c := RelPoint.post (T_ℓ) _ ∘ jac.aj`"
    above is the record of what went wrong; the statement now carries a second
    existentially bound datum `e : RelPoint jstr (𝟙 SpecQ)` and the recipe clause
    reads
    
        c [d] = ∑_k aj [d/D_k] + e
    
    with `e` pulled back to `Spec ℚ̄` along `specAlgClos ℚ`.  This is the `Γ₁`
    transport of `X0.lean`'s cluster repair of 2026-07-30, which that file's
    `exists_heckeCorrespondenceFamily` explicitly asks for ("**THE Γ₁ TWIN IS
    STILL UNREPAIRED** … the repair transposes verbatim").
    
    **THE DEFECT.**  Write `[·]` for `IsCoarseModuliY1.classify` pushed into `X`
    and `aj x = [x] − [o]`.  The honest witness `c := T_ℓ ∘ aj` gives
    `c [d] = T_ℓ[d] − T_ℓ[o]`, while the unrepaired recipe demanded
    `∑_k aj [d/D_k] = T_ℓ[d] − (ℓ+1)[o]`.  The two agree exactly when
    
        ε := T_ℓ[o] − (ℓ+1)[o] = 0,
    
    i.e. when the correspondence fixes the base point.  And the old statement did
    not merely fail for that one `c`: it was UNSATISFIABLE whenever `ε ≠ 0`.  Given
    any `c` with the naturality and base-point clauses, `IsJacobianOf.universal`
    returns `u` with `RelPoint.post u _ ∘ aj = c`; subtracting the recipe at `d`
    from the recipe at `d'` cancels the `−(ℓ+1)[o]` and yields
    `u ([d] − [d']) = T_ℓ ([d] − [d'])`, so `u = T_ℓ` on the subgroup generated by
    differences of non-cuspidal `ℚ̄`-points, which is all of `J_1(N)(ℚ̄)`; the
    recipe at a single `d` then reads `T_ℓ[o] = (ℓ+1)[o]`, i.e. `ε = 0`.
    
    **`X0.lean`'s WITNESS DOES NOT TRANSPORT, AND THE SENTENCE THERE THAT SAYS IT
    DOES IS WRONG.**  That file says "the same witness refutes them (the base-point
    defect is a statement about the correspondence, not about the level
    structure)".  The DEFECT does transport; the WITNESS does not, and a reader who
    took the sentence at face value would conclude this leaf is true.  The `Γ₀`
    witness is `N = 37`, `ℓ = 2`, `o` a NON-CUSPIDAL rational point of `X₀(37)`
    with `[o] − [∞]` of infinite order.  **`X_1(N)` has no such point.**  A
    non-cuspidal rational point of `X_1(N)` is a pair `(E, P)` with `P` of exact
    order `N` over `ℚ`, and by Mazur's torsion theorem those exist only for
    `N ≤ 10` and `N = 12` — precisely the `N` for which `X_1(N)` has genus `0`, so
    `J_1(N) = 0` and `ε = 0` trivially.  For every `N` of positive genus
    (`N = 11` and `N ≥ 13`) the rational points of `X_1(N)` are exactly its
    rational CUSPS, which is where the `Γ₀` audit stopped looking: it records
    "`ε = 0` DOES hold for every rational cusp", and that is a `Γ₀` fact.
    
    **IT FAILS AT `Γ₁` AT THE CUSPS, WHICH IS WHY THE LEAF IS STILL FALSE.**  On
    `X₀(N)` the cusp `∞` is fixed by the correspondence with multiplicity `ℓ + 1`,
    because the `Γ₀`-structure `μ_N ⊂ E_q` is carried to `μ_N` by every one of the
    `ℓ + 1` isogenies.  A `Γ₁`-structure is a POINT, and the isogenies move it.
    Write the cusps of `X_1(N)` on the Tate curve `E_q = ℚ̄((q^{1/N}))^*/q^ℤ`:
    
    * `c_a := (E_q, q^{a/N})`, the `0`-type cusps, `a ∈ (ℤ/N)^*/±1`;
    * `c'_a := (E_q, ζ_N^a)`, the `∞`-type cusps.
    
    The `ℓ + 1` order-`ℓ` subgroups are `μ_ℓ` and the `ℓ` groups
    `⟨ζ_ℓ^i q^{1/ℓ}⟩`.  Quotienting by `μ_ℓ` is `z ↦ z^ℓ`, which sends
    `q^{a/N} ↦ (q^ℓ)^{a/N}` and `ζ_N ↦ ζ_N^ℓ`; quotienting by
    `⟨ζ_ℓ^i q^{1/ℓ}⟩` is the inclusion into `E_{q^{1/ℓ}}`, which sends
    `q^{a/N} ↦ (q^{1/ℓ})^{aℓ/N}` and fixes `ζ_N`.  Hence
    
        T_ℓ [c_a]  = [c_a] + ℓ [c_{aℓ}],        T_ℓ [c'_a] = [c'_{aℓ}] + ℓ [c'_a],
    
    so `ε(c_a) = ℓ ([c_{aℓ}] − [c_a])` and `ε(c'_a) = [c'_{aℓ}] − [c'_a]`.  Both are
    nonzero as soon as the two cusps are distinct, i.e. as soon as
    `ℓ ≢ ±1 (mod N)`.
    
    **THE WITNESS: `N = 11`, `ℓ = 2`, `o` a rational cusp of `X_1(11)`.**
    `X_1(11)` has genus `1` and IS the elliptic curve `11a3` (`y² + y = x³ − x²`),
    so `J_1(11) = X_1(11)` and `J_1(11)(ℚ) ≅ ℤ/5ℤ`.  `X_1(11)` has `10` cusps, `5`
    of them rational, and by Mazur those `5` are ALL of `X_1(11)(ℚ)` — so the group
    `ℤ/5ℤ` is generated by differences of rational cusps.  Take `o` to be one of
    them.  Since `2 ≢ ±1 (mod 11)`, the cusp `o` is moved, and on a genus-`1` curve
    with a base point `[P] − [Q] = 0` iff `P = Q`, so the difference is a NONZERO
    element of `ℤ/5ℤ`; `ℤ/5ℤ` has no `2`-torsion, so multiplying it by `ℓ = 2`
    does not kill it either.  Hence `ε(o) ≠ 0` on both cusp families, and the
    unrepaired statement is refuted.  (This is a cleaner witness than the `Γ₀` one:
    `J` is an elliptic curve, so no Manin–Drinfeld or infinite-order input is
    needed — the whole computation is inside a group of order `5`.)

    forcing step needs the pin to be non-vacuous, i.e. at least one `d` over
    `Spec ℚ̄` carrying a full family of `IsGamma1Isogeny`.  That is the inhabitation
    question recorded on `IsModularHeckeActionGamma1` above, and it is NOT settled.
    The repair is safe in both regimes: the new statement is strictly WEAKER than
    the old one (take `e := ab.zero (𝟙 SpecQ)` to recover it), and in the vacuous
    regime the leaf is cheap either way.  What would overturn this audit is a proof

ITS OWN DOCSTRING, quoted so you can judge before opening the file --
treat its ROUTE and its cost estimates as HYPOTHESES (they were written
before anyone tried), but its FALSITY AUDITS as binding until you refute
them yourself.  An absence claim ('not in mathlib', 'nowhere stated') is
scoped to the import cone and the DATE it was written -- re-grep it:

    /-- **THE BASE-POINT-FREE REDUCTION: a nonconstant map to an abelian variety
    DESCENDS from an extension over which the curve acquires a rational point**
    (sorry leaf, NEW 2026-07-30) — the second residue of
    `exists_nonconstant_toAbelianScheme_of_notGeometricallyRational` below, and
    the ONLY place where the missing section is still owed.
    
    It is the exact statement of the gap that leaf's audit names first: Abel–Jacobi
    `x ↦ [x] − [o]` needs a `K`-rational base point, and a smooth proper
    geometrically connected curve over `K` need not have one — a genus-`1` curve
    with `C(K) = ∅` is the standard witness.
    
    TRUE, by the classical repair.  `hconn` makes `C` nonempty, and `C` is of
    finite type over `K` by `hproper`, so it has a closed point; `C` is smooth over
    `K`, so it has a closed point whose residue field `L` is a FINITE SEPARABLE
    extension of `K` (the `K^sep`-points of a smooth `K`-scheme are dense).  The
    graph of that point is an `L`-rational point of `C_L`, so `hsec L` applies and
    gives an abelian variety `A/L` with a nonconstant `c : C_L ⟶ A`.  Weil
    restriction `Res_{L/K} A` along the finite étale `L/K` is then an abelian
    variety over `K`, the unit `C ⟶ Res_{L/K}(C_L)` is a `K`-morphism, and the
    composite `C ⟶ Res_{L/K}(C_L) ⟶ Res_{L/K}(A)` is the required map.  It is
    nonconstant because base changing it to `L` and composing with the counit
    `(Res_{L/K} A)_L ⟶ A` recovers `c`, and a constant map stays constant under
    both operations.
    
    **WHAT A PROVER MUST BUILD**: Weil restriction along a finite locally free
    morphism, and the fact that it preserves `AbelianSchemeStruct`.  That is the
    whole residue, and it does not exist at this pin — checked 2026-07-30 with
    `grep -rniE "weil.?restriction" Fermat/ .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/`,
    which returns NOTHING.  (Do not run the check as
    `grep restrictScalars` instead: that returns two dozen hits in
    `Modularity/HeckeFrameForm.lean`, all of them `Submodule.restrictScalars`,
    which is module theory and has nothing to do with the scheme-level
    construction.)  Separability of `L/K` is what makes
    `Res_{L/K} A` SMOOTH, which is why the paragraph above insists on a closed
    point with separable residue field rather than an arbitrary one.
    
    **FALSITY AUDIT — `hsec` IS NOT VACUOUS AND IS NOT THE CONCLUSION.**  The
    tempting reading is that `hsec` at `L = K`, `ℓ = 𝟙`, already IS the
    conclusion, making this leaf trivial.  It is not: `hsec` is only usable at an
    `L` for which `C_L` HAS an `L`-rational point, and the whole difficulty is
    that `L = K` need not be such an `L`.  Conversely `hsec` is not vacuous —
    its consumer discharges it, for every `L` at once, from
    `exists_nonconstant_toAbelianScheme_of_hasNoFibreAffineLine` above.
    
    **`hproper`, `hsmooth`, `hconn` ARE ALL LOAD-BEARING**, and each for a
    different step: `hconn` for nonemptiness, `hproper` for finite type (hence a
    closed point with finite residue extension), `hsmooth` for separability of that
    extension.  Dropping `hsmooth` does not obviously refute the statement, but it
    removes the only reason `Res_{L/K} A` is smooth, so it is not decoration.
    
    **RELOCATION NOTE**, as for the two theorems above: nothing here is `Γ₁`- or
    even modular-specific, and `X0.lean`'s open
    `exists_nonconstant_toAbelianScheme_of_one_le_x0Genus` would consume it

morphisms of the generic fibres, so they extend uniquely over `𝒪ᵥ`, and uniqueness makes
the extensions compatible with composition.

THE FACT (it is TRUE): the lattice `L_g = ℤ + ℤτ_g ⊂ ℂ`, where `τ_g = formPoint g hg` is the root of
`a X² + bX + c` in `ℍ`, is homothetic to the proper `ℤ[√−n]`-ideal
`𝔞 = ℤ·a + ℤ·((−b + √(−4n))/2)`; for a PRIMITIVE form of discriminant `−4n` its multiplier ring is
exactly the order of discriminant `−4n`, i.e. `ℤ[√−n]` (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Lemma
7.5 and Theorem 7.7). The complex torus `ℂ/L_g` is an elliptic curve with `j = j(τ_g)` and
`End = ℤ[√−n]`, and since `j(τ_g)` is algebraic it descends to `ℚ̄` with endomorphism ring
unchanged. Cox §§10–11; Silverman *ATAEC* VI.3 for the uniformisation, II.1.2 for the
endomorphism-ring computation.

    `Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/NumberTheory/BinaryQuadraticForm.lean` (already `public import`ed): `j(z)`
    is an ALGEBRAIC INTEGER whenever `z ∈ ℍ` satisfies a nontrivial integral quadratic relation.

    theory: `complexEmbedding` (defined just above the target) is `IsAlgClosed.lift`, whose image is
    an algebraically closed subfield of `ℂ` containing `ℚ`, hence contains every algebraic number.

    the shape that works is: `range complexEmbedding` is algebraically closed (it is the injective

    an algebraically closed field, hence of degree 1, hence `j(τ_g) ∈ range`.

the curve to `ℚ̄` with endomorphism ring unchanged. Item (iii) is worth cutting out even if you get

STATEMENT. For `ab : AbelianSchemeStruct jstr` with `jstr : J -> SpecQ` and a prime `p`: there is a FINITE `S : Finset ND` of rational primes such that for every rational point `P : RelPoint jstr (id SpecQ)`, every geometric point `y` with `p . y = ratToGeom jstr P`, and every prime `q` not in `S`,

i.e. every element of `localInertiaGroup hq.toHeightOneSpectrumRingOfIntegersRat`, pushed into `Gamma_Q` along `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup.map`, fixes `y`.

WHAT WAS DONE ON 2026-07-31 AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR YOU. This leaf was cut out of `exists_ramificationSet_geomPtField`, which is now PROVEN over it (commit 6437d52d). ALL the field theory is discharged, so do not redo any of it:
  * `exists_isGalois_fixingSubgroup_divisionSet` (PROVEN, X0.lean) manufactures a finite GALOIS `L/Q` whose fixing subgroup is EXACTLY the subgroup of `Gamma_Q` fixing every `p`-division point of `P` at once. It works because the division set is `Gamma_Q`-STABLE (rationality of `P`, via `galSMul_ratToGeom`) and FINITE (a torsor under `A[p]`).
  * `not_dvd_subfieldDiscr_of_inertiaTrivialAt` (PROVEN, X0.lean) turns inertia-triviality on a Galois `L` into `q` not dividing `discr K` for every subfield `K`, over the dictionary in `Fermat/FLT/GaloisRepresentation/InertiaUnramified.lean` (hoisted 2026-07-31 for exactly this) and mathlib's `NumberField.discr_dvd_discr`.
So your conclusion is the cheapest possible shape: you only have to move ONE inertia subgroup onto ONE division point. Do NOT widen the quantifier from `localInertiaGroup` to all of `Gamma_Q` -- that is FALSE as soon as `Q(y) != Q`, which is the generic case, and it is the standing trap recorded in CLAUDE.md.

THIS IS A SWEEP, NOT A PROOF TASK, AND IT HAS ALREADY PAID FOR ITSELF TWICE.

The defect class: a block is hoisted out of a giant module into a NEW module, the
new module is `public import`ed back, and the ORIGINALS are never deleted.  Every
duplicate is then a hard `has already been declared`.  `tools/merge/semmerge.py`
propagates ADDITIONS and never DELETIONS, so no later merge can remove them, and
the errors are invisible to `lake build`, to the `declaration uses 'sorry'`
warning set and to every frontier scan whenever a module upstream is red
(CLAUDE.md's SEVENTH invisibility class).

TWO CONFIRMED INSTANCES, both release blockers, both found by accident:
  * `FreyCurve/MazurTorsion.lean` vs `IsogenySignature.lean` and `X0.lean` — 249

    duplicates, the whole Cohen/Witt coefficient-ring block, hoist commit
    `759621e8`.  Fixed by `flt-lean-337` on 2026-07-31; that file is now GREEN.

WHAT TO DO.  Enumerate every pair (A, B) of project modules where A `public
import`s B, and intersect their top-level declaration-name sets.  `tools/merge/
xdup.py .` does the qualified pass; a 20-line python name-intersection over a
declaration regex is enough and is what found the `PatchingWitt` case.  Prioritise
modules created in the last two weeks (`git log --diff-filter=A --since=...
--name-only -- 'Fermat/**/*.lean'`), since a hoist is the usual reason a new
module appears next to a giant one.

FOR EACH HIT, COMPARE BODIES BEFORE DELETING ANYTHING.  Normalise whitespace and
strip comments, then diff the two copies.  IDENTICAL means the deletion is
mechanical and nothing is being chosen between — delete the DOWNSTREAM copy, i.e.
the one in the file doing the importing.  DIFFERENT means the downstream copy may
have been improved after the hoist and deleting it would silently revert that
work; decide each one and say in the commit message which way and why.  In the
`PatchingWitt` case all 28 shared bodies were identical.

A PARTIAL TRIM IS A TELL: `Patching.lean` had already lost `wittVectorTopology`
while keeping the other 27, so it was USING one hoisted name and REDECLARING the
rest.  If you find one name removed and its neighbours not, expect a whole block.

(`~/.flt-release-lake/build/lib/lean`) into ONE farm directory — a two-entry
LEAN_PATH does NOT fall through, this was measured — rebuild any module missing

  LP=$(lake env printenv LEAN_PATH | sed 's#<worktree>/.lake/build/lib/lean#<farm>#')

TARGET: sweep the tree for OTHER semmerge-orphaned superseded blocks — code with
no consumer that a declaration-level merge preserved and that no frontier instrument can see

Work in {{FLT_WORKTREE}}, on its same-named branch.

  export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH"
  git rev-list --count HEAD..main    # must be 0, else: git merge --ff-only main
  # if your target files live only on `merger` (release window), `git merge --ff-only merger`

WHY THIS EXISTS.  `tools/merge/semmerge.py` iterates over THEIRS' declarations and splices
them into OURS.  There is NO code path in it that removes a declaration from OURS.  So when a
branch REPLACES a block — deleting the old one and adding a new one — the merge keeps BOTH.
The added half is checked by every instrument in the tree; the orphaned half is checked by
none, because it still compiles.  It has no `sorry`, no error, it is reachable from
`Fermat.lean`, and it is not free-floating in the census sense.  Its only cost is build time,
and nothing in this development measures build time per module.

ONE CONFIRMED INSTANCE, ALREADY CLEANED (2026-07-31, `flt-lean-347`), as the worked example:
`MazurNonCMFrobenius.lean`'s hand-rolled `namespace F1` .. `namespace F5` Frobenius chain plus
the whole sibling module `MazurNonCMFrobeniusB.lean` — 4 601 lines, superseded by the
generated `MazurNonCMFrobenius/ElevenA.lean` and `.../ElevenB.lean`, with no consumer anywhere
in the tree.  Measured on cyclops: `lake build Fermat.FLT.EllipticCurve.MazurNonCMCertificate`
went from 944 s to 429 s, and the module count from 2072 to 2071.  Both builds green with the
same four `sorry`s.  Read that commit ("DELETE the superseded F1-F5 Frobenius certificates")
for the exact method before starting.

THE METHOD, which is the whole task.

1. Find REPLACEMENT-shaped merges.  `git log --diff-filter=M --stat` over the release merges,
   looking for a branch that ADDED a module under `X/` while the merge left `X.lean` at its
   old size; and `tools/merge/xdup.py` / `tools/merge/dupstmt.py`, which already look for
   cross-file duplicate declarations — a superseded block that was NOT deduplicated is the
   residue those tools leave behind after the duplicates are removed.  Generated modules are
   the highest-yield place to look: grep for `GENERATED by` and for the `gen_*.py` scripts at
   the repo root, and compare what each generator emits TODAY against what is committed.

2. Prove no consumer, three ways, all of them.  A grep is not enough on its own.
   (a) grep the whole tree for the MODULE name — if nothing outside the file and its
       importers mentions it, the candidate set is just those importers;
   (b) for each importer, check NAMESPACE RESOLUTION, not just text: a sibling namespace
       under a common prefix cannot be reached by a bare name, which is what made the
       `ElevenA`/`ElevenB` case safe;
   (c) a COMMENT-STRIPPED token scan of every declared name in the region over the whole
       tree — strip nested `/- -/` and `--` first, or docstrings will manufacture hits.
   Also grep the region for `@[simp]` and any other attribute: an attributed lemma can be
   reached by a tactic without appearing in any proof term, and then no name scan can see it.

3. MEASURE BEFORE AND AFTER.  Build the affected cone from a warm `.lake` before the deletion
   and after it, and require the SAME `sorry` set both times (line numbers may shift; the
   declaration names must not).  Put both timings in the commit message — that number is the
   entire justification for the change, and nobody can reconstruct it later.

4. If the deleted code was GENERATED, mark its generator SUPERSEDED in the same commit and
   name the replacement.  `flt-frobenius-cert.py` still had `--out
   Fermat/FLT/EllipticCurve/MazurNonCMFrobenius.lean` in its usage example and claimed
   regenerating that module "reproduces it byte for byte"; re-running it would have overwritten
   the live shared machinery and broken both generated row modules.

CRITICAL, AND THE REASON THIS TASK CAN SILENTLY PRODUCE NOTHING: your branch will be a
DELETION.  `semmerge` cannot carry a deletion, so if the merge worker runs it on your files
your entire branch merges to a no-op AND THE MERGE REPORTS CLEAN.  Say so in `to_merger`,
explicitly, naming every file and every declaration block you removed, and ask for plain
`git merge`.  See the CLAUDE.md section "A DELETION-ONLY BRANCH IS INVISIBLE TO `semmerge`".

A FULL RESULT INCLUDES FINDING NOTHING.  If the sweep turns up no further orphaned block,
say which merges and which generated modules you checked and how — that list is what stops
the next agent repeating the search.  Do NOT delete anything you cannot show has no consumer;
a wrong deletion here is a build break, and the payoff is only wall-clock.

THE STATEMENT:

    theorem exists_riemannRochGrowth_of_effectiveDivisorCount {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime]
        {X : Scheme.{0}} (strX : X ⟶ _root_.Fermat.SpecF q) [IsProper strX]
        [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 strX] [GeometricallyConnected strX] :
        ∃ g h : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 * g ≤ n + 1 →
          (q - 1) * effectiveDivisorCount strX n + h = h * q ^ (n + 1 - g)

where `effectiveDivisorCount strX n = Nat.card (EffectiveDivisorOfDegree strX n)` and
`EffectiveDivisorOfDegree strX n = {D : X → ℤ // IsDivisorOn X D ∧ (∀ z, 0 ≤ D z) ∧ divisorDegree (k := ZMod q) strX D = (n : ℤ)}`,
both defined immediately above it and both using the vocabulary of
Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/CurveGenus.lean.

THIS IS THE RIEMANN–ROCH THEORY BUILD. Do not expect to close it in one sitting and do
not grind. The most valuable outcome is a further DECOMPOSITION into named sorried
leaves with compiling glue. The leaf's own docstring in the file is long and carries
the full route, the pin survey with file:line, and the suggested next cut — READ IT,
it is the task specification and it is more detailed than this prompt.

THE ONE FINDING YOU MUST NOT LOSE. The bound `2 * g ≤ n + 1` (i.e. `n ≥ 2g−1`) is SHARP
and is genuinely required. `Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/CurveGenus.lean`
carries `IsCurveGenus` / `exists_isCurveGenus`, which is RIEMANN'S theorem
(`ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g` for `deg D ≥ B`, `B` unspecified), and its docstring asserts
"Nothing in the two consumers needs the sharp bound". THAT IS NOW FALSE and this leaf is
the counterexample: `g` and `h` are pinned by the conclusion, since over ℤ the identity
reads `h·q^{1−g}·q^n − h = h₀·q^{1−γ}·q^n − h₀` and two sequences `A·q^n + B` with
`q ≥ 2` agreeing infinitely often force `A = A'` and `B = B'`. So you cannot buy a
weaker bound by enlarging `g`, and Riemann's inequality does not suffice — you need
Riemann–Roch proper (`ℓ(D) − ℓ(K−D) = deg D + 1 − g` with `ℓ(K−D) = 0` for
`deg D > 2g−2`), hence a canonical divisor, hence duality. Sanity check: at `g = 1`,
`n = 1` gives `(q−1)·A₁ + h = h·q` with `A₁ = #E(𝔽_q) = h` ✓, while `n = 0` would give
`(q−1) + h = h`, false.

WHAT IS IN THE PIN, and it is much more than the pre-2026-07-31 surveys of this leaf
said — the divisor theory landed during release 29, all reachable from Interface.lean
through `ModularCurve/X0.lean`:
  * CurveGenus.lean — `rrSet`, `ell` (ℓ(D)), `divisorDegree`, `IsDivisorOn`,
    `pointDivisor`, `IsCurveGenus`, `IsCurveGenus.unique` (PROVEN), `exists_isCurveGenus`
    (leaf).
  * PrincipalDivisorDegree.lean — `Scheme.Hom.divCoeff/divDegree/zeroDegree/poleDegree`,
    `finite_divSupport` (PROVEN), and `divDegree_eq_zero` (PROVEN: a principal divisor
    has degree zero — usually the expensive step, and it is already done).
  * CurveDivisorDegree.lean — `ord_inv`, `ord_div`, `divDegree_mul`, `divDegree_inv`.
  * CurveExtension.lean — `isIntegral_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_geometricallyConnected`
    (PROVEN). YOU WILL NEED THIS FIRST: `Scheme.ord`, hence `rrSet`, hence `ell`, needs
    `[IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]`, which the statement deliberately does NOT
    carry (carrying it would push the obligation onto every consumer). Derive them; the
    second is mathlib's `LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian strX`.
  * mathlib has NO Riemann–Roch and no divisor group. `FunctionField.classNumber` is NOT
    the `h` here — it is the class group of the ring of integers, not the degree-zero
    DIVISOR class group. Wiring it in as if it were is a faithfulness trap.

SUGGESTED CUT, in the order the glue wants: (i) linear equivalence of divisors and the
fact that `deg` descends to classes (over the PROVEN `divDegree_eq_zero`); (ii) the
single clause `∃ h, ∀ n : ℤ, #{classes of degree n} = h`, which encodes BOTH finiteness
of the degree-zero class group AND surjectivity of `deg` onto ℤ (F. K. Schmidt) and is
exactly what the counting consumes; (iii) `#{effective divisors in [D]} = (q^{ℓ(D)}−1)/(q−1)`,
stated subtraction-free as `(q−1)·N + 1 = q^{ℓ(D)}`; (iv) sharp Riemann–Roch,
`deg D ≥ 2g−1 → ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g`. Final assembly is a `Nat.card` fibration of
`EffectiveDivisorOfDegree` over the `h` classes.

THE STATEMENT:

    theorem eulerCount_eq_effectiveDivisorCount {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] {X : Scheme.{0}}
        (strX : X ⟶ _root_.Fermat.SpecF q) [IsProper strX]
        [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 strX] [GeometricallyConnected strX] (n : ℕ) :
        eulerCount (closedPointDegreeCount strX) n = effectiveDivisorCount strX n

THIS IS THE EASY HALF of the Riemann–Roch step and it is deliberately separated from the
hard one — do NOT try to prove any Riemann–Roch here. It is pure bookkeeping: an
effective divisor is a finitely-supported nonnegative ℤ-valued function on the
codimension-one points, i.e. exactly a multiset of closed points, and grouping that
multiset by degree turns the count into the Euler-product coefficient
`coeff n ∏_{d=1}^{n} (1 − T^d)^{−b_d}`. No genus, no class group, no Riemann–Roch.

DEFINITIONS INVOLVED, all in the same file or in CurveGenus.lean:
  * `eulerCount b n = PowerSeries.coeff n (eulerPartial ℕ b n)`, with
    `eulerPartial R b N = ∏_{d ∈ Ioc 0 N} (eulerGeomFactor R d)^(b d)` and
    `eulerGeomFactor` written as `Σ_k T^{dk}` in ℕ⟦T⟧ (no subtraction anywhere).
    `coeff_eulerPartial_stable` gives stationarity in `N` from `N = n` on.
  * `closedPointDegreeCount strX d = Nat.card {x : X // pointResidueDegree strX x = d}`,
    with `pointResidueDegree strX x = Module.finrank (ZMod q) κ(x)` for the algebra
    structure `strX` induces.
  * `EffectiveDivisorOfDegree strX n = {D : X → ℤ // IsDivisorOn X D ∧ (∀ z, 0 ≤ D z) ∧ divisorDegree (k := ZMod q) strX D = (n : ℤ)}`,
    `effectiveDivisorCount strX n = Nat.card` of it. `IsDivisorOn X D` is
    `(Function.support D).Finite ∧ ∀ z, D z ≠ 0 → coheight z = 1`, and
    `divisorDegree strX D = ∑ᶠ z, D z * (strX.residueDegree z : ℤ)` — both from
    Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/CurveGenus.lean.

THE TWO IDENTIFICATIONS THAT ARE NOT `rfl`, and they are the whole cost:
  1. `pointResidueDegree strX x` (finrank over `ZMod q` of κ(x)) against
     `strX.residueDegree x` (mathlib's `[κ(x) : κ(strX x)]`), which is what
     `divisorDegree` weights a point by. They agree because `Spec (ZMod q)` has ONE point
     with residue field `ZMod q`, but that is a computation with
     `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.residueDegree`, not an unfolding.
  2. `coheight z = 1` (CurveGenus.lean's notion of a codimension-one point) against
     `pointResidueDegree strX z ≠ 0`. The generic point has infinite residue field, hence
     `pointResidueDegree = 0` (`Module.finrank`'s junk value — and `0 ∤ s` for `s > 0` is
     exactly why the point counts already ignore it). The direction needing work is that a
     coheight-one point has FINITE residue degree, which is where properness enters; the
     file already has the finiteness in a weaker form as `finite_pointsOfResidueDegree`,
     over `_root_.Fermat.finite_relPoint_of_isProper`.

A GOOD DECOMPOSITION IS A FULL SUCCESS HERE TOO: e.g. one leaf for each of the two
identifications above, one for `EffectiveDivisorOfDegree strX n ≃ (multisets of closed
points of total degree n)`, and the Euler-product coefficient computation as proven glue.

THE QUESTION. Found 2026-07-31 while cutting
`exists_rigidifiedModuliSchemeData_of_isUnit`, and NOT created by that cut --
it is as old as `CyclicSubgroupOfOrder`.

`CyclicSubgroupOfOrder ab N` asks for a finite flat closed subgroup scheme whose
GEOMETRIC FIBRES are cyclic of order N. It does NOT ask that its rank be N. Its
own docstring justifies the substitution by Cartier's theorem -- "a finite flat
group scheme is etale, so its rank equals the number of points of any geometric
fibre" -- but Cartier's theorem needs the ORDER to be invertible on the base, and
the order is exactly what is not being pinned. The justification is circular.

THE CONCRETE OBJECTS IT LETS IN. Over a base of characteristic p with p not
dividing N and p not dividing n -- which satisfies every hypothesis of
`exists_rigidifiedModuliSchemeData_of_isUnit` and of both leaves under it -- take
E over F_p-bar ordinary with Z/N contained in E[N]. Then C = (Z/N) x mu_{p^k} is
finite, flat, a closed subgroup scheme, contains the zero section, is closed
under the group law and inversion, and its geometric relative points are exactly
Z/N, cyclic of order N -- for EVERY k >= 0. (The inclusion is legitimate: for
ordinary E the connected part of E[p^infinity] over F_p-bar is mu_{p^infinity},
and gcd(N, p) = 1 makes the sum direct.) So `Gamma0Datum N (Spec F_p-bar)` has
infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic inhabitants above each honest one, and
the functor those leaves assert is representable is strictly larger than
Katz-Mazur's [Gamma_0(N)].

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and why this is a question and not a refutation: that
the enlarged functor is NON-representable. The extra objects are separated from
the honest ones by the locally constant rank of C, so a representing object
could a priori be a disjoint union indexed by that rank. Refuting it wants the
SUPERSINGULAR locus: for ordinary E the connected order-p^k subgroup is the
canonical mu_{p^k} and is unique, and for supersingular E the order-p one is
ker F and is unique, but higher connected subgroups of E[p^k] are not -- a
fibre that jumps over a connected base is the shape of the argument, and it is
the same shape as the `(P_0 + eps*v, Q_0)` refutation this cluster already
survived once.

WHAT TO DO -- DECIDE IT, EITHER WAY, AND ACT. Do not leave it open.

  * If the enlarged functor IS non-representable, then every leaf in this file
    quantifying over `Gamma0Datum N T` at positive characteristic is FALSE AS
    STATED. The repair is to `CyclicSubgroupOfOrder`, NOT to the leaves: add a
    rank clause, or the "etale-locally isomorphic to Z/N" / "admits a generator"
    clause that Katz-Mazur actually use -- exactly as the earlier repair added
    `nsmul_P`/`nsmul_Q` to `FullLevelStructure` rather than restating its
    consumers. Check the blast radius first
    (`grep -n "CyclicSubgroupOfOrder" Fermat/FLT/ModularCurve/X0.lean`), and note
    that `CyclicSubgroupOfOrder.ofDvd` already carries an
    `[AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (c.ι ≫ f)]` instance argument -- evidence that the
    missing clause has been felt before.
  * If the enlargement is HARMLESS (the functor is still representable, or the
    junk objects cannot occur for another reason), say so with the argument and

THE MATHEMATICS — two independent things must be produced.

(1) EXISTENCE of ONE elliptic curve over `ℚ̄` whose geometric endomorphism ring is
    the order of discriminant `−4n`. Two routes:
    (a) analytic (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §§10–11): the lattice
        `ℤ + ℤτ` with `τ = (−b + √(−4n))/(2a)` from `f = ⟨a, b, c⟩` has multiplier
        ring exactly that order BECAUSE `f` is primitive; `j(τ)` is algebraic, so
        the curve is definable over `ℚ̄`;
    (b) algebraic (Silverman *ATAEC* II): start from any curve with CM by the
        order and pass to `E/E[𝔞]` for a proper `O`-ideal `𝔞`. Given the Vélu
        machinery above, (b) is likely much cheaper here than (a); what is
        genuinely absent is proper ideals of a NON-MAXIMAL order, not the
        quotient construction.

(2) IRRATIONALITY of its `j`. `hne` says the form class group of the order is
    nontrivial, i.e. `h(−4n) ≥ 2`. The `h(−4n)` CM `j`-invariants of the order are
    the roots of one irreducible polynomial over `ℚ` (`K(j)` is the ring class
    field), so each has degree `h ≥ 2` over `ℚ`, hence is irrational.

CHECK THE CHEAPER ROUTE FIRST. The sibling leaf
`exists_algEquiv_apply_eq_of_isCMJInvariant` (`Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` acts TRANSITIVELY on the
CM `j`-invariants of one order — the first main theorem of CM) is still open in
the same file. Modulo it, this leaf is EQUIVALENT to the old
`∃ x y distinct` form: transitivity turns `x ≠ y` into "`x` is moved by some `σ`",
hence irrational; and stability turns irrationality back into a distinct pair.

or whether assuming the sibling makes this one cheap — one owner closing both is

# Fermat/FLT/FreyCurve/MazurTorsion.lean

TARGET: `exists_isCusp_ne_post_of_atkinLehnerPin` -- inside `section AtkinLehnerModelCut`,
immediately above `exists_genericFibreAut_of_atkinLehnerModel`. Locate by NAME.

This is ATKIN-LEHNER (1970) 2 ON THE CUSPS and NOTHING ELSE. It was cut out of
`exists_isCusp_ne_neronGenAut_of_atkinLehnerPin` on 2026-07-31 (which is now PROVEN over it),
and the cut removed the entire integral model from the statement: no `q`, no `R`, no `toF`,
no special fibre, no `IsX0JNeronDatum`, no `w`/`w_Y`/`hcomm`/`hinv`/`hgen`. What is left is:

  hc  : IsCoarseModuliY0 N strY          -- Y = Y_0(N) over Q
  hX  : IsCompactificationY0 strY strX   -- X smooth proper over Q, Y a dense open
  hN  : 1 < N
  al  : AtkinLehnerMorphism N
  wYQ : Y -> Y, hwYQ : wYQ >> strY = strY
  hpin: wYQ realises the moduli action `al.dual` on the coarse space, at every test scheme
  v   : X -> X, hv : v >> strX = strX      -- a Q-MORPHISM OF SCHEMES
  hvj : hX.j >> v = wYQ >> hX.j            -- v extends wYQ across the cusps
  hvinv : v >> v = 1_X
  CONCLUSION: exists c : RelPoint strX (1 SpecQ), hX.IsCusp c and RelPoint.post v hv c /= c

WHY IT IS TRUE. `w_N` exchanges the cusps above `e` and `N/e`, hence the cusps `1` and `N`,
i.e. `oo` and `0`. Both are Q-rational (`gcd(1,N) = gcd(N,1) = 1`, so `phi(gcd) = 1`, and
`residueQDegree_eq_totient` in `X0.lean` makes the residue field `Q`) and they are distinct for
`1 < N`. So `w_N` moves `oo`.

DO NOT DELETE `al` OR `hpin`. The leaf is FALSE without them: `v := 1_X` makes `hvj` read
`hX.j = wYQ >> hX.j`, and `hX.j` is a mono (`hX.isOpenImmersion`), so `wYQ = 1_Y`; `hpin` then
forces `w_N` to act trivially on `Y_0(N)`, false at every `N > 1`. The docstring carries this
audit in full; read it.

DO NOT weaken `v` to an abstract involution of `X(Q)`. That cut is FALSE and the counterexample
is in the docstring: `hX.IsCusp` is BY DEFINITION "not in the image of `Y(Q)`", so the moduli
action on the image together with the IDENTITY on the cusps satisfies every hypothesis. What
kills it here is that `v` is a MORPHISM OF SCHEMES and `Y` is dense in the separated `X`, so `v`
is the unique extension of `wYQ`. That is the only role the old integral model played.

`hvinv` is retained DEFENSIVELY and is not believed necessary; the sole call site holds it. If
your proof does not use it you may delete it together with the one argument at the one call site
in `exists_isCusp_ne_neronGenAut_of_atkinLehnerPin`.

WHAT IS IN THE TREE AND WHAT IS NOT, checked 2026-07-31.
`X0.lean` has the whole cusp-indexing layer -- `exists_cuspResidueIndexing`,
`residueQDegree_eq_totient`, `nonempty_cuspLocus`, `nonempty_cuspIndexing_of_ne_zero`,
`IsX0Compactification.CuspLocus`, `IsX0Compactification.CuspIndexing` -- and every one of them
is stated over `IsX0Compactification N strX strY j`, NOT over `IsCompactificationY0`. You have
`hX : IsCompactificationY0 strY strX` plus `hc`, which is three fields short of an
`IsX0Compactification`: `connected : GeometricallyConnected strX`, `finite_compl`, and
`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 strX` (you only have `Smooth strX`). So the FIRST step is almost
certainly to build that bridge -- see the companion queued task, or do it inline. The template

those fields from `isSmoothCurve_of_isCoarseModuliY0`,

`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSmoothCompactification_of_isAffine`; the difficulty is that you are
handed `X` rather than constructing it, so you must derive the three fields for the GIVEN `X`

What is genuinely NOT in the tree is the ACTION of `w_N` on the cusps -- the `e -> N/e`

# Fermat/FLT/ModularCurve/X0.lean -- a missing bridge that unlocks the cusp layer

TASK: prove
  theorem nonempty_isX0Compactification_of_isCompactificationY0 {N : Nat} (hN : 0 < N)
      {Y X : Scheme.{0}} {strY : Y -> SpecQ} {strX : X -> SpecQ}
      (hc : IsCoarseModuliY0 N strY) (hX : IsCompactificationY0 strY strX) :
      Nonempty (IsX0Compactification N strX strY hX.j)
(name and exact shape are yours to choose; `Nonempty` because the structure is data).

WHY. `X0.lean` carries the whole Q-side cusp layer -- `exists_cuspResidueIndexing`,
`residueQDegree_eq_totient`, `nonempty_cuspLocus`, `nonempty_cuspIndexing_of_ne_zero`,
`IsX0Compactification.CuspLocus`, `card_compl_range_le_card_divisors` -- and every one of them
is stated over `IsX0Compactification`. Several consumers, including the Atkin-Lehner cusp leaf
`exists_isCusp_ne_post_of_atkinLehnerPin` in `MazurTorsion.lean` and everything in
`IsX0JNeronDatum`'s generic-fibre half, hold only `IsCompactificationY0 strY strX` plus
`IsCoarseModuliY0 N strY`, and therefore cannot reach any of it. Today each such consumer would
have to re-derive the gap itself.

WHAT IS MISSING. `IsCompactificationY0` gives `j`, `over`, `isOpenImmersion`, `isDominant`,
`proper`, `smooth : Smooth strX`. `IsX0Compactification` additionally needs
`smooth : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 strX`, `connected : GeometricallyConnected strX`, and
`finite_compl : (Set.range j.base)^c.Finite`. All three are statements about a GIVEN `X` that
happens to be a smooth proper compactification of `Y_0(N)`, and none of them is modular.

THE TEMPLATE, and it is most of the work already done: the proof of `exists_x0Compactification`
(`X0.lean`, ~line 41399) assembles exactly these three fields, but for the `X` it CONSTRUCTS.
It uses `isSmoothCurve_of_isCoarseModuliY0` (properties of `Y_0(N)`, including geometric
connectedness), `isAffine_of_isCoarseModuliY0`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSmoothCompactification_of_isAffine` and
`geometricallyConnected_of_isSmoothCompactification`, all in
`Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/CurveCompactification.lean`. Its own docstring says the
two extra clauses "come from the general theory and not from anything modular: geometric
connectedness is inherited from `Y_0(N)` along a dense open immersion, and finiteness of the
cusp locus is finiteness of the complement of a dense open in an irreducible curve." Those two
sentences are the two proofs you need, for an arbitrary `X` rather than the constructed one.

TWO ROUTES, and pricing both before starting is the task's first step.
(a) DIRECT: prove the three fields for the given `X` from `hX` and `Y`'s properties.
(b) TRANSPORT: get an `IsX0Compactification` for the CONSTRUCTED compactification from
    `exists_x0Compactification`, then transport along the unique isomorphism of
    compactifications over `Y` (uniqueness of the smooth compactification of a curve). This
    needs a transport lemma for `IsX0Compactification` along an iso commuting with `j`, which
    may be worth having anyway -- but note it also forces you to transport `IsCusp`, `RelPoint`
    and any morphism the consumer holds, which is why (a) is probably cheaper for consumers.

DO NOT add the three fields to `IsCompactificationY0` instead. That structure is consumed all
over `X0.lean` and `MazurTorsion.lean` and is deliberately the weaker interface; strengthening
it makes every PRODUCER harder and is the opposite trade.

`lake` is NOT on PATH: `export PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH`. `X0.lean` is ~100k lines and its
build is ~40 min when green; develop in a scratch module that `public import`s it.

      ∧ (∀ (W : Y.Opens) (hW : W ≤ U) (r : Γ(Y, W)), r * Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op s = 0 → r = 0)
      ∧ (∀ (W : Y.Opens) (hW : W ≤ U) (x : Γ(Y, W)), σ.app W x = 0 → ∃ r : Γ(Y, W), x = r * Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE hW).op s)

In words: near `σ(t)` the ideal sheaf of the section is generated by a single nonzerodivisor `s`. This is Stacks 0C4S / EGA IV 17.12.1. Note `Γ(sectionIdeal σ, W)` IS `ker (σ.app W)` — that is `sectionIdealMap_app_eq_zero_iff`, PROVEN just above the leaf — so the three clauses really are the ideal-sheaf statement and there is NO sheaf-of-modules category theory left in this leaf.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, and the one place to consider splitting further. `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 strY` unfolds (mathlib `AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Smooth.lean`) to: for each `y : Y` there are affine opens `U' ⊆ T` and `V ⊆ strY ⁻¹ᵁ U'` with `y ∈ V` and `(strY.appLE U' V _).hom` STANDARD SMOOTH of relative dimension 1. Take `y = σ.base t`. On such an affine `V = Spec B` over `A = Γ(T, U')`, the section gives an `A`-algebra retraction `B ↠ A` whose kernel `I` is the ideal; standard smoothness of relative dimension 1 makes `I/I² ≅ Ω_{B/A} ⊗_B A` free of rank 1 over `A`, so `I` is generated by one element after shrinking, and that element is a nonzerodivisor because `B` is `A`-flat with regular one-dimensional fibres.

The two clauses are quantified over EVERY open `W ≤ U`, not over a basis. That is deliberate and it is NOT extra mathematics: given the affine case, `hnzd` is exactly what makes the local cofactors `rᵢ` agree on overlaps, so they glue, and `x = r·s` then follows by separatedness of `Γ(Y, -)`. **If that gluing turns out to cost more than ~100 lines, cut it off as its own PROVEN lemma beside `nonempty_sectionIdeal_restrict_iso_of_generator`** — it is a statement about a nonzerodivisor in a sheaf of rings with no geometry in it, it belongs there rather than here, and it would leave this leaf quantified only over the affines of a cover. THE ROUTE, and the three ingredients are independent enough to be attacked in any order.
Write `S := Z.ringCatSheaf.obj`, `R := W.ringCatSheaf.obj`, `L := presheafModPullback h`.

1. `L ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj U)) ≅ (free R).obj (yoneda.obj (h ⁻¹ᵁ U))`.

   `PresheafOfModules.pushforwardCompCoyonedaFreeYonedaCorepresentableBy phi U` corepresents
   `N ↦ ((free S).obj (yoneda.obj U) ⟶ (pushforward phi).obj N)` by

   counterexample in the section header destroys — do not try to prove it for a general
   site, it is FALSE there.

   `m := PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaEquiv.symm (ModuleCat.freeMk ι ⊗ₜ ModuleCat.freeMk ι')`
   where `ι : U ⊓ U' ⟶ U`, `ι' : U ⊓ U' ⟶ U'`; then prove `IsIso m` sectionwise (a
   `PresheafOfModules` morphism all of whose `app`s are isos is an iso — build the inverse
   with `PresheafOfModules.isoMk`, whose naturality obligation is `m.naturality` itself).
   Sectionwise at `V` the poset makes it a two-case split, with NO Finsupp combinatorics
   beyond `Finsupp` on a subsingleton: `Hom(V,U)` in `Opens` is `ULift (PLift (V ≤ U))`.
     - `V ≤ U ⊓ U'`: all three Hom-types are singletons, both sides are `S(V)`, and the map
       sends the basis element to `1 ⊗ₜ 1`.
     - otherwise: the source is `Free(∅) = 0`, and at least one factor of the target is too
       (`V ≤ U` and `V ≤ U'` would give `V ≤ U ⊓ U'`), so the target is `0`.
   `finsuppTensorFinsupp'` (`Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/DirectSum/Finsupp.lean`) gives

With 1–3 both source and target of `delta` are isomorphic to
`(free R).obj (yoneda.obj (h ⁻¹ᵁ (U ⊓ U')))`. THE REAL WORK IS THEN SHOWING THAT `delta`
ITSELF IS THAT ISOMORPHISM — two objects being abstractly isomorphic proves nothing about a
given map between them, and this is where the effort will go. The cheapest shape found so
far, which avoids computing `delta` on elements (you cannot: `pullback` has no formula):

* `Adjunction.leftAdjointOplaxMonoidal_δ` gives
  `delta P Q = (adj.homEquiv _ _).symm ν` with `ν = (adj.unit.app P ⊗ₘ adj.unit.app Q) ≫ μ (pushforward phi)`.
* Hence by `Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right`, `adj.homEquiv (delta ≫ g) = ν ≫ (pushforward phi).map g`.
  So `g ↦ delta ≫ g` is bijective for every `N` iff `g ↦ ν ≫ (pushforward phi).map g` is.
* A map `f : A ⟶ B` with `g ↦ f ≫ g` bijective for every `N` is an iso: surjectivity at
  `N = A` gives `g` with `f ≫ g = 𝟙`, then `f ≫ (g ≫ f) = f ≫ 𝟙` and injectivity at `N = B`
  gives `g ≫ f = 𝟙`. Five lines; write it as a standalone lemma.
* Now use `PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaEquiv` and `freeYonedaEquiv_comp`
  (`freeYonedaEquiv (m ≫ φ) = φ.app _ (freeYonedaEquiv m)`, which is `rfl`) to turn both
  hom-sets into `N.obj (op (h ⁻¹ᵁ (U ⊓ U')))`, at which point the claim reduces to ONE
  element identity that does not mention `N`: that `ν` composed with the step-2 generator
  of `(P ⊗ Q).obj (op (U ⊓ U'))`, namely `freeMk ι ⊗ₜ freeMk ι'`, equals the step-1/step-2
  generator on the `W` side. `μ (pushforward phi)` is sectionwise `m₁ ⊗ₜ m₂ ↦ m₁ ⊗ₜ m₂`
  (`ModuleCat.restrictScalars_μ_tmul`), and `adj.unit.app P` applied to `freeMk ι` is
  `(pushforward phi).map ι` applied to `adj.unit.app P (freeMk 𝟙)` by naturality — and
  `adj.unit.app P (freeMk 𝟙)` is what step 1's `uniqueUpToIso` formula computes.

   THE METHOD, and the receipt that makes a relocation safe in a file with a dozen
   concurrent editors:
     1. collect the declaration names in the region the block would jump over;
     2. strip comments from the block and tokenise with `isalnum() or c in "_'."` --
        NOT a unicode range, `A-￿` swallows the anonymous-constructor brackets;
     3. if the intersection is empty the move is legal;
     4. after moving, assert the file's SORTED LINE MULTISET is unchanged and its length
        is unchanged.  That is what proves a pure permutation; `git diff --stat` does not,
        because git realigns large moves and reports inflated insert/delete counts.
   Release 30 did exactly this for the 246-line block and it took ten minutes.

WHAT IT IS. One step of the level-shrinking descent. You are given: the full Galois package of the cluster (an `l`-adic `rho` over `O` with residual `rhobar` hardly ramified and irreducible, linked by `hpi`; a totally real Galois `F` with `hirrF`; a coefficient field `E`, a bad set `badF`, an abstract Hecke polynomial function `heckeF`, and `hmod` matching `charFrob` of `rho|_{G_F}` against `heckeF` at every `w` outside `badF`); a `U(1)` level datum `S_cal : TotallyDefiniteQuaternionAlgebra.U1Data F E p` with `S_cal.Q = empty`; a NONZERO weight-2 form `f` on `D^x` of level `U1 S_cal` which is a simultaneous `T_w`-eigenvector for every `w` outside `S_cal.S` with eigenvalue `a w`, matching `-(heckeF w).coeff 1` off `badF`; a place `w0` IN `S_cal.S`; and the LOCAL ramification input `hsw0 : (rho.map (algebraMap Q F)).IsUnramifiedAt w0`. You must produce a nonzero eigenform at the level `S_cal.eraseS w0` -- i.e. the same datum with `w0` removed from `S`, which by `U1`'s definition means the local level at `w0` becomes the FULL level `GL2(O_{w0})` -- with the same eigenvalue matching off `badF`.

So in one sentence: UNRAMIFIED AT `w0` IMPLIES SPHERICAL AT `w0`.

THE CLASSICAL ARGUMENT, in three steps, none of which is currently in this tree:
  1. STRONG MULTIPLICITY ONE identifies the automorphic representation `pi` generated by `f` with the one attached to `rho|_{G_F}`: `hmod` pins the eigenvalue `a w` against `tr rho(Frob_w)` at every `w` outside `S_cal.S union badF`, a set of density one, and `hirrF` makes the match rigid.
  2. LOCAL-GLOBAL COMPATIBILITY at `w0` turns `hsw0` into "`pi_{w0}` is unramified". Note nothing here places the divisors of `l` inside `badF`, so the `l`-adic Hodge-theoretic half of local-global compatibility is genuinely needed when `w0 | l`.
  3. THE LOCAL NEWVECTOR STATEMENT at `w0`: an unramified `pi_{w0}` has a nonzero `GL2(O_{w0})`-fixed vector. Its `T_{w0}`-eigenvalue is the one local-global compatibility predicts, which is the `w = w0` case of the conclusion's last conjunct (vacuous if `w0` is in `badF`).

WHAT IS IN THE TREE AND USABLE, verified 2026-07-31 rather than summarised:
  * `TotallyDefiniteQuaternionAlgebra.U1Data.eraseS` and its three lemmas (`mem_eraseS_S`, `eraseS_Q`, `card_eraseS_S_add_one`) are PROVEN, in `KhareWintenberger.lean` just above this leaf. They are pure bookkeeping and there is nothing left to do there.

    /-- **THE ONE OPEN LEAF OF THIS FILE (2026-07-31, RECUT): the characteristic-`2` count at
    a SUPERSINGULAR TARGET, `W'.a₁ = 0`.**
    
    `exists_wronskianPoly_scalar_charTwo_coprime` below is now PROVEN over this, and this is
    all that is left of it.  In characteristic `2` an elliptic curve has `a₁ = 0` exactly when
    it is supersingular (`j = 0`), and `lineOfDiff_ne_zero_of_charTwo` then forces `a₃′ ≠ 0`,
    so the hypothesis `ha₁'` says `T := a₁′A + a₃′B` degenerates to `a₃′·B` and the conclusion
    degenerates to `P·S = c·a₃′·B²`, i.e. `u′·S = c·a₃′` for `u = A/B` — "the invariant
    derivation `D = S·d/dX` sends `u` to a CONSTANT".
    
    **WHY THIS CASE AND NO OTHER.**  When `a₁′ ≠ 0` one has `T = a₁′·(A − r′B)` with
    `r′ = a₃′/a₁′`, so `T` is a Wronskian-companion of `B` — `wronskianPoly_sub` says the pair
    `(A − r′B, B)` has the SAME Wronskian `P` as `(A, B)` — and the two crude bounds
    `rootMultiplicity_le_wronskianPoly_left/_right`, sharpened by `charTwo_even_pow_dvd_derivative`
    at the places where `hparB`/`hparT` supply an even multiplicity, give

    When `a₁′ = 0` the companion collapses: `T = a₃′B`, so the requirement at a pole of `u`
    (`m := ord_b B > 0`) is the DOUBLED `2m ≤ ord_b P + ord_b S`, and neither crude bound nor

    at `∞` when `deg A > deg B`.
    
    **THE DERIVATIVE IDENTITY THE ROUTE NEEDS IS COMPILER-VERIFIED (2026-07-31) — PASTE IT.**
    It is not specific to `a₁′ = 0` and it costs nothing but this text; it is not committed as a
    declaration only because nothing in the cone would consume it until this leaf is proven.
    Differentiate `hcurve`, eliminate `G′` with the ring identity
    `B·G′ = (A² + a₄′B²)·P + B′·G` (`P = A′B − AB′`, true over any commutative ring), and fold
    `E²G` back to `B³N` by `hcurve` itself; the `B³B′N` terms cancel and what is left is
    
        B⁴ · N′  =  E² · (A² + a₄′B²) · P ,
    
    with `N = Cx²f + D² + Cx·D·S` the bracket of `hcurve`.  In Lean, verbatim and green:
    
        theorem charTwo_derivative_curveEq (h2 : (2 : F) = 0) {A B Cx D E : F[X]}
            (hcurve : B ^ 3 * (Cx ^ 2 * (X ^ 3 + C W.a₂ * X ^ 2 + C W.a₄ * X + C W.a₆) + D ^ 2
                + Cx * D * (C W.a₁ * X + C W.a₃))
              = E ^ 2 * (A ^ 3 + C W'.a₂ * A ^ 2 * B + C W'.a₄ * A * B ^ 2 + C W'.a₆ * B ^ 3)) :
            B ^ 4 * (Cx ^ 2 * (X ^ 2 + C W.a₄) + derivative Cx * D * (C W.a₁ * X + C W.a₃)
                + Cx * derivative D * (C W.a₁ * X + C W.a₃) + Cx * D * C W.a₁)
              = E ^ 2 * (A ^ 2 + C W'.a₄ * B ^ 2) * (derivative A * B - A * derivative B) := by
          have h2p : (2 : F[X]) = 0 := by
            have h : (C (2 : F) : F[X]) = 0 := by rw [h2, map_zero]
            rwa [map_ofNat] at h
          have hd := congrArg derivative hcurve
          simp only [derivative_add, derivative_mul, derivative_pow, derivative_C,
            derivative_X, zero_mul, zero_add, add_zero, Nat.cast_ofNat,
            Nat.add_one_sub_one, mul_one, map_ofNat, pow_one] at hd
          linear_combination B * hd - derivative B * hcurve
            + (-(B ^ 4 * (Cx * derivative Cx * (X ^ 3 + C W.a₂ * X ^ 2 + C W.a₄ * X + C W.a₆)
                  + Cx ^ 2 * (X ^ 2 + C W.a₂ * X) + D * derivative D))
              - B ^ 3 * derivative B * (Cx ^ 2 * (X ^ 3 + C W.a₂ * X ^ 2 + C W.a₄ * X + C W.a₆)
                  + D ^ 2 + Cx * D * (C W.a₁ * X + C W.a₃))
              + B * E * derivative E * (A ^ 3 + C W'.a₂ * A ^ 2 * B + C W'.a₄ * A * B ^ 2
                  + C W'.a₆ * B ^ 3)
              + B * E ^ 2 * (A ^ 2 * derivative A + C W'.a₂ * A * derivative A * B
                  + C W'.a₄ * A * B * derivative B + C W'.a₆ * B ^ 2 * derivative B)) * h2p
    
    `map_ofNat` in that `simp only` is load-bearing: without it `derivative_pow` leaves `C 2`
    and `C 3` in `hd`, `ring` treats them as ATOMS unrelated to the numerals `2`, `3`, and the
    `linear_combination` fails with a residual full of `C 3 * … - … * 3`.
    
    **WITH THAT IDENTITY THE COUNT CLOSES AT EVERY FINITE `b` WITH `S(b) ≠ 0`** — checked by
    hand 2026-07-31, and it is the bulk of the leaf.  Fix such a `b` with `m := ord_b B > 0`
    (if `m = 0` there is nothing to prove, `T = a₃′B`), so `A(b) ≠ 0` by `hcop` and `G(b) ≠ 0`:
    
    * `hone` cancelled by `B` reads `a₃′·E = Cx·S`, so `x := ord_b E = ord_b Cx`;
    * `hcurve` gives `3m + ord_b N = 2x`, hence `ord_b N < 2x`, hence
      `charTwo_AS_rootMultiplicity` applies and `ord_b N = 2·ord_b D`; so `m` is even (this is
      `charTwo_rootMultiplicity_B_even`, i.e. `hparB`) and `d := ord_b D = x − 3m/2`;
    * the identity above gives `4m + ord_b N′ = 2x + ord_b(A² + a₄′B²) + ord_b P`, and
      `ord_b(A² + a₄′B²) = 0` because `A(b) ≠ 0` while `ord_b(a₄′B²) = 2m > 0`;
    * the four terms of `N′` have orders `≥ 2x`, `≥ x − 1 + d`, `≥ x + d − 1`, `≥ x + d`
      (`pow_sub_one_dvd_derivative_of_pow_dvd` for the two derivatives, `ord_b S = 0` here), so
      `ord_b N′ ≥ x + d − 1 = 2x − 3m/2 − 1`;
    * therefore `ord_b P ≥ 4m − 3m/2 − 1 = 5m/2 − 1 ≥ 2m`, the last step because `m` is even
      and positive, so `m ≥ 2`.  That is exactly the doubled bound the parent cannot reach.
    
    `N′ ≠ 0` is free: if it vanished the identity would force `P = 0` (`A² + a₄′B² ≠ 0`, since
    over an algebraically closed field of characteristic `2` it is `(A + √a₄′·B)²`, and `A = cB`
    with `A`, `B` coprime makes `B` a unit and `P = 0`), and `P = 0` is the trivial branch.
    
    **SO EXACTLY TWO PLACES ARE LEFT, and a prover should be sent at those and nothing else:**
    
    1. **the root `b₀` of `S`** (only when `a₁ ≠ 0`) **at which `B` also vanishes.**  There

       `ord_{b₀} E = ord_{b₀} Cx + 1`.  The requirement is the weaker `2m ≤ ord_{b₀} P + 1`,
       and the identity above reduces it to `ord_{b₀} N′ ≥ 2·ord_{b₀} Cx + 1 − 2m`, for which
       the missing input is a lower bound on `ord_{b₀} D` — the analogue of the
       Artin–Schreier step at a ramified place.  Geometrically `b₀` is the `2`-torsion point of
       `W`, and `B(b₀) = 0` says it lies in the kernel, so this is a real configuration

    /-- **The self-pair value computation at an ARBITRARY level** (sorry leaf, cut
    2026-07-31 out of `weilValueProp_self_of_even_of_ne_two` below; Silverman *AEC*
    III.8.1(b)): in any admissible Miller setup for the self-pair of a `p`-torsion
    point `P`, the value `z` is `1`.
    
    This is the exact level-`p` analogue of `weilValue_two_torsion_config_eq_one`
    above — same engine hypotheses, same configuration, same value equation, with
    `2` replaced by `p` and the `2`-torsion input `⊖P = P` replaced by the honest
    torsion hypothesis `htor : p•P = 0`.  It is stated for EVERY `p` and therefore
    SUBSUMES the `p = 2` node (which is PROVEN independently, by the line-square
    factorization, and is deliberately left resting on its own proof: rerouting a
    proven theorem through a `sorry` would only enlarge the sorried cone).
    
    **WHAT THE VALUE EQUATION SAYS.**  Write `v_S := XClass x_S`, `v_R := XClass x_R`
    and read the ideal clauses as divisors on the affine curve:
    `div aP = p(P⊕S) + p(⊖S)`, `div v_S = (S) + (⊖S)`, so
    
        g_S := aP / v_S^p     has     div g_S = p(P⊕S) − p(S),
    
    and likewise `g_R := aQ / v_R^p` has `div g_R = p(P⊕R) − p(R)`.  Dividing `heq`
    through by the four vertical factors turns it into the Miller cross-ratio
    
        z = g_S(D_R) / g_R(D_S),     D_R := (P⊕R) − (R),  D_S := (P⊕S) − (S),
    
    which is `e_p(P, P) = f_P(D_P')/f_{P}(D_P)` in Silverman's notation.
    
    **WHY NOTHING FORMAL CLOSES THIS, AND WHY THE SWAP CANNOT.**  Let `f` be the
    untranslated Miller generator, `div f = p(P) − p(O)`; then `g_S = c·(f ∘ τ_{⊖S})`
    for a constant `c`, and substituting gives, with `W := R ⊖ S` and
    `Ψ(V) := f(P⊕V)/f(V)`,
    
        z = Ψ(W) / Ψ(⊖W).
    
    So the ONLY thing the configuration is symmetric under is `W ↦ ⊖W`, which
    inverts `z` — i.e. the swap construction of `exists_weilPairing_mu` extracts
    exactly `z² = 1` and can never do better.  Nor can the algebra downstream:
    `B((x₁,x₂),(y₁,y₂)) = x₁y₂ − x₂y₁ + 2x₁y₁` over `ZMod 4` is bilinear, skew
    (`B(x,y) + B(y,x) = 4x₁y₁ = 0`), nondegenerate (determinant `1`) and has
    `B(x,x) = 2x₁² ≠ 0` for odd `x₁`, so bilinearity + skew-symmetry +
    nondegeneracy + `μ_p`-valuedness do not imply alternation at even level.  (The
    swap construction does prove genuine skew-symmetry `e(x,y)·e(y,x) = 1` for a
    general pair, independently of alternation — it is only stated for self-pairs
    in `exists_weilPairing_mu` because that is all the μ-proof needed.  The
    counterexample above says that adding it changes nothing.)  Nor does level
    compatibility `e_m(nP, nQ) = e_{mn}(P, Q)^n`: at `4 ∣ p` it reads
    `e_2(·,·) = e_p(P,P)^{p/2} = 1`, which is vacuous.  Alternation at even level
    is a GEOMETRIC input.
    
    **ROUTE 1 — THE TWO-TORSION TRANSLATE (cheapest, and BLOCKED only by a
    genericity clause; re-examine this before starting Route 2).**  Suppose the two
    auxiliary translates differ by a NONZERO `2`-torsion point, `R = S ⊕ t`,
    `2t = O`.  Then `⊖t = t`, so
    
        div (τ_t^* aP) = p(P⊕S⊖t) + p(⊖S⊖t) = p(P⊕R) + p(⊖R) = div aQ,
        div (τ_t^* v_S) = (S⊖t) + (⊖S⊖t) = (R) + (⊖R)         = div v_R,
    
    whence `aQ = c·τ_t^*(aP)` and `v_R = c'·τ_t^*(v_S)` for constants `c, c'`
    (units of the coordinate ring are constants — `hCunits`).  Since

    cancel between numerator and denominator.  So `z = 1` on the nose, at EVERY
    level and with no `p`-division point anywhere.  The divisor transport is not
    hand-waving: it is `WeilPairing.spanSingleton_pointEval_translate`
    (`WeilPairingDescent.lean`, PROVEN),
    `span(τ_Q^* b) · I_{⊖Q}^{|D|} = ∏_{X ∈ D} I_{X ⊖ Q}`.
    
    WHAT BLOCKS IT, EXACTLY: `weilValueProp` demands `x_S ∈ F'` and `x_R ∉ F'`.

    /-- **`det ρ_{E,n} = χ_n`: THE DETERMINANT OF THE GALOIS ACTION ON `E[n]` IS THE
    MOD-`n` CYCLOTOMIC CHARACTER** (sorry leaf, cut 2026-07-31 out of
    `exists_weilPairing_mu_nondeg_of_natCast_ne_zero` below, which is now a PROVEN
    assembly over it).
    
    Stated elementarily and without any cyclotomic-character API: for every
    `k`-automorphism `σ` of `k̄` and every primitive `n`-th root of unity `ζ ∈ k̄`,
    
        `σ ζ = ζ ^ (det (σ | E[n])).val`.
    
    Since `σ ζ = ζ ^ χ_n(σ)` DEFINES `χ_n(σ) ∈ (ℤ/n)ˣ` (mathlib:
    `ModularCyclotomicCharacter`), this says precisely `det ρ_{E,n} = χ_n`.  The
    determinant is taken of the `ZMod n`-linear endomorphism of `E[n]` induced by
    `σ`; `E[n]` is free of rank two by `WeierstrassCurve.n_torsion_dimension`
    (which is where `(n : k) ≠ 0` is spent a second time), so the determinant is not
    a junk value.
    
    QUANTIFIER NOTE.  `ζ` is universally quantified, but the statement for ONE
    primitive root implies it for all: any other is `ζ ^ j` with `j` coprime to `n`,
    and both sides are `j`-th powers.  So a prover may prove it at a single
    convenient `ζ` and transport.
    
    WHY IT IS TRUE, AND HOW TO PROVE IT.  It is Silverman *AEC* III.8.1(a)–(e): the
    Weil pairing `e_n : E[n] × E[n] → μ_n` is alternating, nondegenerate and
    Galois-equivariant, so `σ` scales it by `det(σ)` on the source and by `χ_n(σ)`
    on the target.  Two routes are visible from this file (both discussed at length
    in the module docstring): reduce `k` to a finitely generated field and import
    the tree's `ℚ`-case Chebotarev argument
    (`WeilPairing.det_galoisRep_eq_cyclotomic`), or generalise the divisor-theoretic
    construction `WeilPairing.exists_weilPairing_mu` off finite fields by replacing
    its finite-subfield genericity device.
    
    FAITHFULNESS.  `(n : k) ≠ 0` forces `n ≠ 0`; at `n = 0` there is no primitive
    `0`-th root of unity in a field other than by the degenerate convention, and
    `E[0] = E(k̄)` is not free of rank two, so the hypothesis is doing real work.
    At `n = 1` both sides are `1`.  At `n = 2` the claim is `σ ζ = ζ` for `ζ = -1`
    and `det ∈ (ℤ/2)ˣ = {1}`, which is true and vacuous.  No hypothesis on `k`
    beyond `char k ∤ n` is needed or true: the statement holds over every field,
    including `k = k̄` where `Aut(k̄/k)` is trivial and both sides are `ζ`. -/
