    /-- **THE DUAL ISOGENY, over `ℚ̄` and at the level of POINTS** (LEAF, cut
    2026-07-31 off `nonempty_isNIsogenyPair_of_gamma0Model` below) —
    **LEVEL-GENERIC**, and the ONLY one of the five with no scheme theory in it.
    
    TRUE, and it should be ASSEMBLY rather than new mathematics: the whole dual
    API already exists and is PROVEN in `Fermat/FLT/EllipticCurve/Isogeny.lean`,
    over exactly the instances available here (`[IsAlgClosed F] [CharZero F]
    [W.IsElliptic]`, all satisfied by `F = AlgebraicClosure ℚ`).  The route, with
    the name of every input:
    
    1. *`φ ≠ 0`.*  `hker` says `ker φ = ⟨g⟩`, a group of order `N` (`hg`).  If
       `φ = 0` then `E(ℚ̄) = ⟨g⟩` is finite of order `N`, contradicting
       `WeierstrassCurve.n_torsion_dimension`
       (`Fermat/FLT/EllipticCurve/Torsion.lean`), which gives
       `E[N+1] ≃+ (ZMod (N+1))²`, a subgroup of cardinality `(N+1)² > N`.
    2. *`deg φ = N`.*  `Isogeny.degree_of_ne_zero` is `Nat.card (ker φ)`, and
       `hker` plus `Nat.card_zmultiples` and `hg` make that `N`.
    3. *`ψ`.*  `Isogeny.dual ⟨φ, hφ⟩ h0`, whose `toHom` is `Isogeny.dualHom`;
       `Isogeny.dual_toHom` and `Isogeny.dualHom_comp` give `ψ (φ P) = deg φ • P
       = N • P` directly.
    4. *`φ ∘ ψ = [N]`.*  `φ` is surjective (`hφ.surjective h0`), so write `Q = φ P`;
       then `φ (ψ (φ P)) = φ (N • P) = N • φ P` by `map_nsmul`.
    5. *`ker ψ = φ(E[N])`.*  Both directions are two lines from (3) and (4) and
       need no counting: `ψ (φ P) = N • P`, so `φ P` is killed by `ψ` exactly when
       `P ∈ E[N]`, and surjectivity of `φ` makes every `Q` of that form.  (The
       `finite_ker` field of `Isogeny.dual` already contains half of this argument
       verbatim — read it before rewriting it.)
    6. *Galois equivariance of `ψ`.*  `ψ` is the UNIQUE map with `ψ ∘ φ = [N]`,
       because `φ` is surjective.  For `σ`, the conjugate
       `ψ^σ := (Point.map σ) ∘ ψ ∘ (Point.map σ⁻¹)` satisfies
       `ψ^σ (φ x) = σ (ψ (φ (σ⁻¹ x))) = σ (N • σ⁻¹ x) = N • x` using `hgal`,
       `map_nsmul` and `WeierstrassCurve.velu_point_map_symm_map`
       (`EllipticCurve/DifferentialCharacter.lean` uses exactly this idiom at
       `isDiffChar_galConj`).  Uniqueness then gives `ψ^σ = ψ`.
    
    **`hN : N ≠ 0` is load-bearing** through step 1 only; at `N = 0` the kernel is
    not finite and `Isogeny.degree` is not the kernel count.
    
    **The check that refutes this leaf**: an isogeny over an algebraically closed
    field of characteristic `0` with no dual.  There is none — that is Silverman
    *AEC* III.6.1, and the characteristic-`p` counterexample recorded in
    `Isogeny.NotIsRationalMapDualHom` is excluded by `CharZero (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`. -/

    /-- **THE WEIERSTRASS CHARTS REALISE EVERY GALOIS-EQUIVARIANT ISOGENY AS A
    MORPHISM OF THE ELLIPTIC SCHEMES** (LEAF, cut 2026-07-31 off
    `nonempty_isNIsogenyPair_of_gamma0Model` below) — **LEVEL-GENERIC**, and this
    is where the geometry of the gate actually lives.
    
    TRUE.  This is the content the 2026-07-28 model clause was added to make
    reachable, stated so that it is reachable: it produces its OWN identifications
    `ε`, `ε'` of the two geometric fibres — the ones induced by the charts — rather
    than being handed identifications it cannot relate to the charts.  That is the
    whole difference between this statement and the unprovable form; see the
    subsection docstring above and `liesIn_congr_of_geomFibreAddEquiv` below.
    
    **Route.**  `hmod : IsWeierstrassModel d.ab E` is an open immersion
    `ι : Spec ℚ[E] ⟶ d.E` over `Spec ℚ` whose range is the complement of the zero
    section (`X0.lean` ~13572).
    
    * *`ε`.*  A `ℚ̄`-point of `Spec ℚ[E]` is a `ℚ`-algebra map `ℚ[E] → ℚ̄`, i.e. an
      affine point of `E` over `ℚ̄`; `ι` carries it into `d.E`, and the origin goes
      to `ab.zero`.  Bijectivity is `range_eq` plus the open immersion being mono.
      ADDITIVITY is rigidity, not computation: two group laws on an abelian scheme
      with the same identity section agree, so the transported chord–tangent law is
      `d.ab`'s (this is the same rigidity that `isAdditiveOn_of_post_zero`, PROVEN
      in `X0.lean`, packages one direction of).  Galois equivariance is free: `ι` is
      defined over `ℚ` and `galSMul` is precomposition with `Spec σ`.
    * *the morphism.*  `hχ.isRationalMap` presents `χ` by rational functions in the
      Weierstrass coordinates, so it is a morphism `Spec ℚ̄[E] ⟶ Spec ℚ̄[E']` away
      from `ker χ`; `hχgal` is Galois descent, giving it over `ℚ`; and it extends
      across the finitely many missing points — the kernel and the origin — by the
      valuative criterion, `d'.f` being proper (`AbelianSchemeStruct.proper`) and
      `d.E` a smooth curve over `ℚ`, hence regular in codimension one.  The
      compatibility `RelPoint.post u hu (ε x) = ε' (χ x)` then holds by construction
      on the chart and at the finitely many added points by continuity/reducedness.
    
    **Both directions are stated in one leaf on purpose.**  Splitting it into two
    applications of a one-directional lemma would return two UNRELATED pairs of
    identifications, and the composite `u ≫ v` could then not be compared with
    `[N]` at all.  The consumer needs `ε`, `ε'` FIXED across the two realisations.
    
    The `∀ χ` shape (rather than a single named isogeny) costs nothing to prove —
    the identifications are built once, before any `χ` is seen — and is what lets
    the sibling leaf `exists_isogenyIsom_of_gamma0Model_isBaseChangeOf` reuse it.
    
    **The check that refutes this leaf**: a Galois-equivariant isogeny of the
    modelled curves that is not induced by any morphism of the elliptic schemes —
    impossible, an isogeny of elliptic curves over `ℚ̄` descending to `ℚ` IS a
    morphism of the `ℚ`-models, and the model clause is precisely the statement
    that those models sit inside `d.E`, `d'.E`. -/

    GALOIS-EQUIVARIANT IDENTIFICATION OF ITS GEOMETRIC FIBRE IS USED** (LEAF, cut
    2026-07-31 off `nonempty_isNIsogenyPair_of_gamma0Model` below) —
    **LEVEL-GENERIC**, and **THIS ONE MAY BE DELETABLE; READ BEFORE ATTACKING IT.**
    
    **What it is.**  This is the `α`-gap of the subsection docstring above, isolated.
    `e` and `ε` are two Galois-equivariant additive equivalences
    `E(ℚ̄) ≃+ GeomFibrePt d.f (𝟙 SpecQ)`; the statement says they see the same
    subset of `E(ℚ̄)` inside the level structure `d.cyc`.  Equivalently:
    `α := ε⁻¹ ∘ e`, a Galois-equivariant additive automorphism of `E(ℚ̄)`,
    preserves the finite subgroup `ε⁻¹(d.cyc(ℚ̄))`.
    
    **TRUE, and the only proof anyone knows is Tate/Faltings.**  `α` commutes with
    `[m]` for every `m` (it is additive), so it restricts to an automorphism of
    `E[ℓ^∞]` compatible with the transition maps, i.e. to a unit of
    `End_{Γ_ℚ}(T_ℓ E)`.  The Tate conjecture for elliptic curves over a number field
    (Faltings) identifies that with `End(E) ⊗ ℤ_ℓ`, and `End_{Γ_ℚ}(E) = ℤ` for every
    `E/ℚ` — including the thirteen `ℚ`-curves with CM, whose CM is defined only over
    the imaginary quadratic field, so the Galois-EQUIVARIANT endomorphisms over `ℚ`
    are still just `ℤ`.  Hence `α` acts on all of `E_tors` by a scalar in `ℤ̂ˣ`, and a
    scalar preserves every subgroup.  **Not available in this tree, in mathlib, or
    in `~/cs/FLT`.**
    
    **THE CHEAPER REPAIR, and it is what a successor should probably do instead.**
    The gap exists only because `IsGamma0ModelOf` asserts the existence of *some*
    Galois-equivariant `e` without tying it to the model clause's chart.  Strengthen
    the pin to say `e` IS the chart identification and this leaf disappears, along
    with its use in the gate.  Concretely, three edits, and the mathematics is
    already there:
    
    1. add to `IsGamma0ModelOf` (above) the clause that `e` agrees with the chart:
       for every affine point `Affine.Point.some x₁ y₁ h`, `(e P).1` is the
       `ℚ̄`-point of `Spec ℚ[E]` at `(x₁, y₁)` composed with the model's `ι`;
    2. `exists_gamma0Model_of_stable` (above, PROVEN) then needs its producer,
       `exists_ellipticScheme_isWeierstrassModel_of_weierstrass` (`X0.lean` ~67199),
       to return an `e` with that compatibility.  It does construct both from one
       source, so this is a strengthening of a STATEMENT, not of a proof — but it is
       in `X0.lean`, upstream of an expensive cone, which is why it was not done
       here;
    3. delete this leaf and the two `liesIn_congr_of_geomFibreAddEquiv` rewrites in
       the gate's proof, which then reads `hlev` directly against `ε`.
    
    Whoever does (1)–(2) should also check the sibling leaf
    `exists_isogenyIsom_of_gamma0Model_isBaseChangeOf` below, which is stated
    against the same pin and inherits the same hole in the opposite direction.
    
    **The check that refutes this leaf**: a Galois-equivariant additive automorphism
    of `E(ℚ̄)`, for `E` over `ℚ`, moving a Galois-stable cyclic subgroup of order `N`

    TRUE, in characteristic zero, and that hypothesis is the whole content.
    
    `ker u` — the fibre product of `u` with the zero section of `d'` — is a closed
    subscheme of `d.E`, and a SUBGROUP scheme, because `u` is additive: `hgeom`
    read at the zero section gives `RelPoint.post u hu (d.ab.zero _) = d'.ab.zero _`
    (the zero section lies in `d.cyc` by `zero_liesIn`), and
    `isAdditiveOn_of_post_zero` (PROVEN, `X0.lean`) upgrades that to additivity.
    `huv : u ≫ v = [N]` bounds it: `ker u ⊆ ker [N] = d.E[N]`, which is finite over
    `Spec ℚ` (`mulByNat` is finite/flat, `AbelianSchemeIsogeny.lean`), so `ker u` is
    a FINITE group scheme over a field of characteristic `0`, hence étale, hence
    REDUCED — this is Cartier's theorem, and it is the one nontrivial input.
    `d.cyc.C` is finite over `Spec ℚ` too (`d.cyc.isFinite`) and reduced for the
    same reason.
    
    Two reduced closed subschemes of a finite-type `ℚ`-scheme with the same
    `ℚ̄`-points coincide, and `hgeom` says exactly that `ker u` and `d.cyc.C` have
    the same `ℚ̄`-points.  So `ker u = d.cyc.C` as closed subschemes, and then for
    an ARBITRARY test point `x : RelPoint d.f g` — non-reduced `T'` included — the
    universal property of the fibre product turns `RelPoint.post u hu x =
    d'.ab.zero g` into "`x` factors through `ker u`", i.e. into
    `RelPoint.LiesIn d.cyc.ι x` (`LiesIn` is literally "factors through", `X0.lean`
    ~836).  No point of the argument is about `ℚ̄`-points once the subschemes are
    identified — which is the point.
    
    **Why `v`, `hv` and `huv` are hypotheses rather than derived**: they are the
    only source of the finiteness of `ker u`, and without finiteness Cartier does
    not apply (a positive-dimensional group scheme in characteristic `0` is smooth
    but this argument would then need `ker u` and `d.cyc.C` to have equal
    DIMENSION, which `hgeom` does not give).  The consumer has them in hand.
    
    **The check that refutes this leaf**: a morphism whose scheme-theoretic kernel
    strictly contains `d.cyc` while having the same geometric points — that is a
    kernel with nilpotents, i.e. an inseparable isogeny, which exists only in
    positive characteristic.  Over `ℚ` there is none. -/

    /-- **LEAF (restated 2026-07-31, flt-lean-249) — THE CLASS POLYNOMIAL
    `H_{−4n}(X) = ∏_{[𝔞] ∈ Cl(ℤ[√−n])} (X − j(𝔞))` EXISTS, HAS RATIONAL
    COEFFICIENTS AND IS IRREDUCIBLE OVER `ℚ`**, stated as: some monic irreducible
    `p ∈ ℚ[X]` vanishes at every CM `j`-invariant of the order `ℤ[√−n]`.
    
    This is Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §11.1, Theorem 11.1 in the form the
    literature actually proves — a CONSTRUCTION (the product above) together with an
    irreducibility statement — and it is the sole remaining leaf of the
    `MazurCMForm` cluster's Galois half. `minpoly_eq_of_isCMJInvariant` below is
    PROVEN from it in two lines, and everything above that is unchanged.
    
    **THE ARGUMENT.** With `K = ℚ(√−n)` and `O = ℤ[√−n]`, the `h(O)` curves with CM
    by `O` have `j`-invariants forming a single `Gal(ℚ̄/K)`-orbit, through the Artin
    isomorphism `Cl(O) ≅ Gal(K(j(𝔞))/K)` of the RING CLASS FIELD; the product
    `H_{−4n}` is then fixed by `Gal(ℚ̄/K)`, and by complex conjugation as well, so it
    lies in `ℚ[X]`, and transitivity makes it irreducible. Silverman *ATAEC* II.4.3
    and II.6.1 is the algebraic presentation of the same theorem. **This is the one
    statement in the cluster that needs the ring class field.**
    
    **IT IS EQUIVALENT TO THE `minpoly` FORM IT REPLACES, NOT STRONGER** — checked
    by proving BOTH directions in a scratch module before the restatement was
    committed, so this is not a hidden strengthening. `⇒` is the proof of
    `minpoly_eq_of_isCMJInvariant` below. `⇐`: if no `x` satisfies
    `IsCMJInvariant n`, take `p = X`; otherwise take `p = minpoly ℚ x₀` for any one
    such `x₀`, which is monic and irreducible because `ℚ̄/ℚ` is algebraic
    (`normal_rat_algebraicClosure` above), and every other CM `j`-invariant is a
    root of it precisely by the `minpoly` form.
    
    **`hn : 0 < n` IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE STATEMENT IS FALSE WITHOUT IT — audit
    re-run 2026-07-31 against THIS statement, since a restatement VOIDS the earlier
    audit (see `CLAUDE.md`).** For `n = −4` the `hsq`/`htop` pair of
    `IsCMJInvariant` is satisfied by `ψ = [2]` on ANY curve with `End = ℤ`, i.e. on
    every non-CM curve over `ℚ̄`: `[2]² = [4] = [−(−4)]`, and `Subring.closure {[2]}`
    contains `1`, hence all of `ℤ = End`. So `IsCMJInvariant (−4)` holds at the
    `j`-invariant of every non-CM curve — and there are INFINITELY many of those
    already among the rationals, since exactly thirteen rational `j`-invariants are
    CM. A monic polynomial is nonzero and so has finitely many roots, so no `p` can
    work: the statement fails outright rather than by a two-element witness, which
    is a sharper refutation than the one the `minpoly` form admitted. The same
    collapse happens at `n = 0`, where `ψ * ψ = 0` forces `ψ = 0`
    (`MazurEndLattice.end_mul_ne_zero`) and `htop` again says `End = ℤ`.
    
    **NOT VACUOUS.** At `n = 1` the curve `y² = x³ + x` has `ψ = i` and `j = 1728`,
    so `p = X − 1728` is forced to be the answer and the statement has content; at
    `n = 5`, `h(−20) = 2` (PARI/GP, re-run 2026-07-31), so `p` must be the quadratic
    `H_{−20}` and a wrong proof can fail.
    
    ## ATOMICITY AUDIT (2026-07-31, flt-lean-249) — DO NOT RE-RUN IT
    
    This leaf admits NO decomposition at this pin that is not either circular or a
    renaming, and the three cuts one naturally reaches for all fail for the SAME
    reason: **the theorem IS the transitivity statement**, so every companion fact
    one might peel off is already available to the step that has transitivity in
    hand. Recorded here so the next owner does not spend a cycle rediscovering it.
    
    1. **Galois STABILITY of `IsCMJInvariant`** — `IsCMJInvariant n x →
       IsCMJInvariant n (σ x)` — does NOT reduce it. Stability says the orbit of `x`
       stays INSIDE the set of CM `j`-invariants; this leaf says the orbit EXHAUSTS
       it. Peeling stability off leaves the whole theorem behind and adds a leaf.
       (It is worth having for other reasons — it collapses the sibling
       `exists_isCMJInvariant_ne_of_not_equivalent` from "produce two distinct CM
       `j`-invariants" to "produce one irrational one" — but not for this one.)
    2. **FINITENESS of the set of CM `j`-invariants** fails the same way, and is
       itself as deep: it is the finiteness of `h(O)`, which needs the
       form-class/ideal-class correspondence, i.e. the sibling leaf's theory.
    3. **The degree route** — `|orbit(x)| = deg_ℚ x` because `ℚ̄/ℚ` is normal and
       separable, so transitivity is equivalent to `deg_ℚ x = |{CM j-invariants}|` —
       is circular in the other direction: the right-hand side is `h(−4n)`, whose
       identification is the SIBLING leaf, and `deg_ℚ x = h(−4n)` is this one.
    
    One tempting intermediate step is also FALSE and was checked rather than
    assumed: **`ℚ(j(𝔟)) ⊆ ℚ(j(𝔞))` does not hold.** The ring class field
    `H = K(j(𝔞))` is normal over `ℚ`, but `ℚ(j(𝔞))` is not — at `D = −23`, `h = 3`
    and `Gal(H/ℚ) ≅ S₃`, so `ℚ(j)` is a non-normal cubic field and does not contain
    its conjugates. So "every CM `j`-invariant lies in the field generated by any
    other" cannot be used to get from one root to all of them.
    
    What genuinely reduces this leaf is a THEORY, not a cut: the ring class field of
    a (possibly non-maximal) order and its Artin isomorphism. Checked against this
    pin on 2026-07-31 and absent: no class group of a non-maximal order (mathlib's
    `ClassGroup` is Dedekind-only), no form class group, no Cox Theorem 7.7, no ring
    class field, no Hilbert class polynomial, no lattices in `ℂ`, no analytic `j`,

    multiplication either.

    whose `j`-invariants have different minimal polynomials over `ℚ` — equivalently,
    a CM `j`-invariant of `ℤ[√−n]` that is not a root of `H_{−4n}`. -/

ITS OWN DOCSTRING, quoted so you can judge before opening the file --
treat its ROUTE and its cost estimates as HYPOTHESES (they were written
before anyone tried), but its FALSITY AUDITS as binding until you refute
them yourself.  An absence claim ('not in mathlib', 'nowhere stated') is
scoped to the import cone and the DATE it was written -- re-grep it:

    /-- **THE FROBENIUS RELATION ON THE TAME QUOTIENT** (LEAF — new 2026-07-31; the
    ONE ingredient the 2026-07-30 tame-character audit on
    `exists_hilbertAuxDiamondQuotient_of_exponents` below identified as genuinely
    absent from `ArtinConductor.lean`).
    
    There is an element `Fr` of the local Galois group at `v` — a lift of the
    arithmetic Frobenius, though the statement does not need to say so — such that
    for EVERY `σ ∈ I_v`,
    
        Fr · σ · Fr⁻¹ · (σ ^ N v)⁻¹  ∈  P_v ,
    
    i.e. `Fr σ Fr⁻¹ ≡ σ^{N v}` modulo WILD inertia, where `N v = #(𝓞_K ⧸ v)` is the
    residue cardinality. This is the defining relation of the tame quotient: `I_v/P_v`
    is `lim_n μ_n(k̄_v)` (`n` prime to the residue characteristic), and a Frobenius
    lift acts on `μ_n` by `x ↦ x^{N v}`.
    
    # WHY IT IS STATED THIS WAY AND NOT THROUGH `tameCharacter`
    
    The classical formulation is `θ(Fr σ Fr⁻¹) = θ(σ)^{N v}` for the tame character
    `θ` of `ArtinConductor.lean`. That form needs a `θ`, hence an `n` and an `X` with
    `Xⁿ` Galois-fixed, and the consumer would then have to identify ITS character
    with `θ` — which is exactly the identification nothing in the hypothesis package
    supplies. The group-theoretic form above needs no character at all: any
    homomorphism out of the decomposition group into a COMMUTATIVE group which kills
    `P_v` converts it into `χ(σ)^{N v − 1} = 1` in one line, and that is the only way
    this development consumes it (see
    `pow_natCard_residue_sub_one_eq_one_of_forall_mem_wildInertiaGroup` immediately
    below). No `n`, no `X`, no compatibility between two tame characters.
    
    # FAITHFULNESS AUDIT (2026-07-31)
    
    *The statement is not vacuous, and `Fr = 1` does NOT discharge it.* With `Fr = 1`
    the clause reads `σ^{1 − N v} ∈ P_v` for every `σ ∈ I_v`, i.e. the tame quotient
    `I_v/P_v` is killed by `N v − 1`. It is not: `I_v/P_v ≅ lim_n μ_n(k̄_v)` contains
    elements of order `n` for EVERY `n` prime to the residue characteristic, and
    `N v − 1` is a fixed integer. So the existential has content and a prover cannot
    dispatch it by choosing a convenient `Fr`.
    
    *It is not vacuously true through an empty index either*: `localInertiaGroup v`
    always contains `1`, and at `σ = 1` the clause is trivially satisfied — which is
    consistent, and is why the audit above is the one that matters.
    
    *The exponent is the RESIDUE CARDINALITY, not `N v − 1` or `ℓ`.* Getting this
    wrong in the other direction would make the leaf false: with `N v` replaced by
    any `m` not congruent to `N v` modulo the (pro-finite) order of `σ`, the relation
    fails already for `σ` of order `n` with `n ∤ (m − N v)`.
    
    *Direction of the conjugation.* `Fr σ Fr⁻¹ = σ^{N v}` is the ARITHMETIC Frobenius
    convention (`Fr` induces `x ↦ x^{N v}` on the residue field). The geometric
    convention gives the inverse exponent; both forms are true for the respective
    lifts, and the statement is an EXISTENTIAL over `Fr`, so it is insensitive to the
    choice — replacing `Fr` by `Fr⁻¹` and `N v` by `N v` is not the same statement,

    `I_v`.

    > Minimality of the presentation puts every Jacobian entry in `𝔪_B`, so
    > `Ω ⊗_B κ ≅ κ^h`; `hfon`'s flatness half then makes `Ω` FREE over the artinian
    > local ring `B̄`, necessarily of rank `h`.  `hΩ` gives `3·B^h ⊆ Jac`, so

    the finite submodule `𝒪₃ᵥ[x₁,…,x_h]` is complete, hence closed, hence all of `B`,
    i.e. `B` is generated as an `𝒪₃ᵥ`-ALGEBRA by the coordinates even though
    `Ω_{R⁄𝒪₃ᵥ}` itself is not finitely generated.

    `hmin` is what makes `Ω ⊗_B κ` have dimension `h` rather than less: it says the
    linear part of every relation has coefficients divisible by `3`, which is the
    only form of minimality the argument uses.

    ## FALSITY AUDIT
    
    `∑_x ord_x(g) · [κ(x) : K] = 0`: a nonzero rational function on a complete curve has as
    many zeros as poles, counted with multiplicity and with residue degree.
    
    TRUE and classical — Hartshorne II.6.10 (stated there for a nonsingular projective curve
    over an algebraically closed field, but the proof is the degree formula for a finite
    morphism and needs neither), Stichtenoth I.4.11, Fulton *Algebraic Curves* §8, and the
    Stacks project's *Algebraic Curves* chapter, which proves it for an arbitrary proper curve
    over a field with `ord` defined by length, i.e. with no normality hypothesis at all.
    
    **NOT VACUOUS, with an explicit witness.**  `X = ℙ¹_ℚ`, `g = t`: `div t = [0] − [∞]`, both
    points `ℚ`-rational, degree `1 · 1 − 1 · 1 = 0`.  A witness where the residue degrees are
    NOT all `1`, which is the case that distinguishes this statement from a naive point count:
    `X = ℙ¹_ℚ`, `g = (t² + 1) / t`.  The zero divisor is the single closed point cut out by
    `t² + 1`, with residue field `ℚ(i)`, so `deg (g)_0 = 1 · 2 = 2`; the pole divisor is
    `[0] + [∞]`, of degree `1 · 1 + 1 · 1 = 2`.  So the theorem is `2 − 2 = 0` and the residue
    degrees are load-bearing in it — a version weighting every point by `1` is FALSE on this
    very example.
    
    **`hproper` IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE LEAF IS FALSE WITHOUT IT**, with the smallest possible
    witness: `X = 𝔸¹_ℚ = Spec ℚ[t]` is integral, Noetherian and smooth of relative dimension
    `1` over `ℚ`, and `g = t` has `div t = [0]`, of degree `1 ≠ 0`.  Every hypothesis except
    `IsProper` holds.  So a successor must not "generalise" this leaf by dropping properness,
    and a consumer that has only an affine curve cannot use it.
    
    **`hcurve` IS *NOT* MATHEMATICALLY LOAD-BEARING, AND IS CARRIED ON PURPOSE.**  The
    statement is true for an arbitrary proper INTEGRAL curve over a field, singularities and
    all, because `Mathlib`'s `Scheme.ord` is built from `Ring.ordFrac` at a Noetherian local
    ring of Krull dimension `≤ 1` — the length-theoretic order, which is exactly the one the
    general theorem is stated for.  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` is carried because
    
    1. both `X0.lean` consumers have it in hand, so it costs them nothing;
    2. it supplies DVR stalks through
       `isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`, PROVEN in
       `Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/CurveExtension.lean`, which is what makes `ord` an
       honest discrete valuation and what every route below actually consumes;
    3. it is what pins the DIMENSION to `1`, and the dimension hypothesis cannot be dropped —
       see the next paragraph.
    
    Removing it is a STRENGTHENING of this leaf, not a repair of it, and a successor who
    removes it should say so rather than silently restate.
    
    **DROPPING THE DIMENSION HYPOTHESIS MAKES THE LEAF VACUOUS, NOT FALSE — and that is the
    trap in this module.**  On a proper integral scheme of dimension `≥ 2` the codimension-`1`
    points have residue fields of positive transcendence degree over `K`, so
    `Scheme.Hom.residueDegree` is `Module.finrank` of an INFINITE extension, which is `0` by
    `Mathlib`'s junk convention.  Every `divCoeff` is then `0` and `divDegree` is `0` for
    trivial reasons.  A "generalisation" of this leaf to arbitrary proper `X` would therefore
    compile, be true, and prove nothing.  The honest higher-dimensional statement is
    `deg(div g · H^{n−1}) = 0` for an ample `H`, which is a different theorem needing
    intersection theory the pin does not have.
    
    **`g ≠ 0` IS NOT NEEDED FOR TRUTH**, and that is why the consumer-facing
    `divDegree_eq_zero` below drops it: `Scheme.ord_zero` gives `ord 0 = 0`, so
    `divDegree strX 0 = 0` outright.  It is kept HERE because every proof route divides by `g`,
    and a prover should not have to carry the degenerate branch through the geometry.

    /-- **The invariants of a finite group acting on a SMOOTH algebra of Krull dimension one
    over a field form a REGULAR ring** (sorry leaf) — Deligne–Rapoport III.1, Katz–Mazur 8.2.1,
    in the ring-theoretic form; classically, "the quotient of a smooth affine curve by a finite
    group is again a smooth affine curve" in the normal-and-one-dimensional formulation.
    
    This is what is left of `X1.lean`'s
    `isRegularRing_tensorAlgebraicClosure_of_isInvariant` once the base change is paid for; see
    that file for the modular consumer and this module's header for what the base change costs
    (nothing — it is `Fermat.InvariantBaseChange.isInvariant_tensor` plus integrality of an
    algebraic extension).
    
    ## THE ROUTE, AND WHY IT IS NOT FIVE LINES
    
    The classical argument is three steps:
    
    1. `S` is smooth over a field, hence REGULAR, hence REDUCED and integrally closed in its
       total quotient ring;
    2. the invariants of a normal ring under a finite group are normal
       (`Algebra.IsInvariant.isIntegrallyClosed_of_isInvariant` in
       `Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/RingTheory/InvariantCoarseRing.lean`), and the Krull dimension is
       unchanged because `R → S` is integral and injective
       (`ringKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral_of_injective`);
    3. normal + Noetherian + dimension one ⇒ regular, which for a DOMAIN is mathlib's
       `[IsDedekindDomain R] : IsRegularRing R`.
    
    **`IsDomain` is the whole difficulty, and it is not available.** `S` here is the base
    change to `k̄` of the coordinate ring of a rigidified moduli scheme, and over a field
    containing `ζ_n` that scheme SPLITS into `φ(n)` components — so neither `S` nor `R` is a
    domain, and both step 2's `isIntegrallyClosed_of_isInvariant` and step 3's Dedekind
    instance carry `[IsDomain R]` at this pin (verified in `InvariantCoarseRing.lean` and in
    `Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean`).
    
    So a prover has to supply, in some form, the **product decomposition**: a reduced normal
    Noetherian ring is a finite product of normal domains, `G` permutes the factors, and the
    invariant ring is the finite product of the invariant rings of the STABILISERS, each of
    which IS a domain and to which the existing lemmas then apply; and a finite product is
    regular iff each factor is.  The same decomposition is written out on
    `transitiveMinimalPrimes_of_gamma1GITPresentation` in `X1.lean`.
    
    ## WHAT IS MISSING FROM THE PIN (measured 2026-07-31, at `a3364fa`)
    
    Three separate absences, each checked by grep rather than recalled:
    
    * **smooth over a field ⇒ regular, or ⇒ integrally closed.**
      `grep -rn 'IsRegularLocalRing\|IsRegularRing' Mathlib/RingTheory/Smooth/ Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/`
      is EMPTY, and `Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/` consists of `Defs.lean` and
      `Polynomial.lean` only — there is no `IsRegularLocalRing → IsIntegrallyClosed` and no
      link to smoothness anywhere.  This tree has the CONVERSE,
      `Algebra.Smooth.of_isRegularRing_of_perfectField`
      (`Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/RingTheory/Smooth/RegularLocal.lean`), and it cannot be run
      backwards.  What this tree DOES have in the forward direction is
      `Algebra.Smooth.isReduced_of_isField`
      (`Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/SmoothReduced.lean`), which is
      reducedness and nothing more.
    * **normality does not localise without a domain.**  Every lemma in
      `Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalProperties/IntegrallyClosed.lean` — `of_localization_maximal`,
      `of_localization`, `of_isLocalization_maximal` — carries `[IsDomain R]`.  So the obvious
      "check regularity prime by prime" reduction of step 3 does NOT go through as stated: one
      can localise `IsNoetherianRing`, `IsReduced` and `Ring.KrullDimLE 1` and not
      `IsIntegrallyClosed`.
    * **no structure theory of reduced normal Noetherian rings.**  There is no
      "finite product of normal domains" statement, and the total quotient ring of a reduced
      Noetherian ring is not known to be artinian here, so the idempotent argument that
      produces the decomposition has to be built.
    
    **The route that DOES look shortest**, and the reason the second bullet is worth recording:
    prove `IsRegularRing` prime-locally after all, and get the domain property at each prime
    from the LOCAL statement *a reduced Noetherian local ring that is integrally closed in its
    total quotient ring is a domain* (its total quotient ring is artinian and reduced, hence a
    finite product of fields; the idempotents are integral over the ring, hence in it; a local
    ring has no nontrivial idempotents, so there is one minimal prime).  Mathlib does have the
    artinian half of that — `IsArtinianRing.equivPi` for a reduced commutative artinian ring,
    and `IsArtinianRing.isField_of_isReduced_of_isLocalRing`.
    
    ## FAITHFULNESS
    
    `hdim` is load-bearing and is where NONDEGENERACY enters: it is consumed as
    `Ring.KrullDimLE 1 S` and is what makes step 3 available at all.  Note that regularity is
    FALSE for invariants in dimension `≥ 2` — `k[x,y]^{±1}`, the quadric cone
    `k[u,v,w]/(uv − w²)`, is normal and not regular — so no proof can avoid using it.
    
    `hinj` is what makes `R` a subring of `S` rather than merely an algebra over it; without it
    take `R := k[x]/(x²) → S := k` with `G` trivial, where `R` is `S^G` in the sense of
    `Algebra.IsInvariant` and `R` is not reduced, let alone regular.
    
    `[Finite G]` is consumed twice: by `Algebra.IsInvariant.isIntegral`, and by the orbit
    grouping in the product decomposition.
    
    The statement is NOT vacuous: `S := k[x]`, `G := ℤ/2` acting by `x ↦ -x`, `R = k[x²]` is an
    inhabitant with `R` regular, and so is any `S` split into several components with `G`
    permuting them. -/

    /-- **THE KEY LEMMA OF FONTAINE'S STEP 3** (sorry leaf, cut 2026-07-31 out of
    `GaloisRepresentation.IsHardlyRamified.exists_pderiv_eq_of_minimalPresentation`):
    *a differential ideal containing `p` is generated by `p` together with the
    elements whose derivatives are all divisible by `p`.*
    
    In the classical formulation — `k` a field of characteristic `p`,
    `R̄ = k[[X₁,…,X_h]]`, `S = k[[X₁^p,…,X_h^p]]` — this says that an ideal of `R̄`
    stable under every `∂/∂Xⱼ` is generated by `𝔞 ∩ S`.  The form below is that
    statement transported back across `R ↠ R/pR`, which is why it needs no field and
    no quotient: `{f | ∀ j, ∂f/∂Xⱼ ∈ (p)}` is the preimage of `S`, and the classical
    `𝔞 = (𝔞 ∩ S)·R̄` becomes `𝔞 = ({p} ∪ (𝔞 ∩ preimage of S))·R`.
    
    PROOF (three steps, no differential equation — an earlier reading of the parent
    leaf guessed that one had to solve `∂u/∂Xⱼ = −u·Cⱼ` over `𝔽₃[[X]]`, and that
    guess is wrong; see the SECOND FALSITY AUDIT on `exists_fontainePresentation`).
    
    1. *Box decomposition.*  Every `f : MvPowerSeries σ 𝒪` is uniquely
       `f = ∑_{a ∈ box} s_a · X^a`, the sum over the finite `box = {a | ∀ j, a j < p}`
       and each `s_a` supported on exponents divisible by `p` (group the monomials of
       `f` by the residue of their exponent mod `p`).  This is an identity over ANY
       commutative ring; no perfectness and no `p`-th roots are involved.
    2. *Maximal-term extraction.*  Write `T^{(b)} := ∏_j (∂/∂Xⱼ)^{b_j}`.  Since each
       `s_a` has all exponents divisible by `p`, `∂ⱼ s_a ∈ (p)`, so by Leibniz
       `T^{(b)}(s_a X^a) ≡ s_a · T^{(b)}(X^a) (mod p)`, and `T^{(b)} X^a = 0` unless
       `a ≥ b` componentwise.  Take `a₀` MAXIMAL for the componentwise order in the
       (finite) set of `a ∈ box` with `s_a ≠ 0`; then every other surviving `a` fails
       `a ≥ a₀`, so `T^{(a₀)} f ≡ (∏_j a₀_j !) · s_{a₀} (mod p)`.  The ideal is
       `∂`-stable, so the left side lies in `𝔞`; `p ∈ 𝔞`; and `∏_j a₀_j !` is a
       product of factorials of naturals `< p`, hence an integer PRIME TO `p`, hence
       invertible mod `p`.  Multiplying by an inverse and correcting by a multiple of
       `p` gives `s_{a₀} ∈ 𝔞`.  This is the only place primality of `p` is used.
    3. *Induction.*  `s_{a₀}` has all its exponents divisible by `p`, so all its
       derivatives lie in `(p)`: it belongs to the generating set.  Replace `f` by
       `f − s_{a₀} X^{a₀} ∈ 𝔞`, whose box support is strictly smaller, and induct on
       the cardinality of that support.
    
    The reverse inclusion is immediate: `p ∈ 𝔞` by hypothesis and the second half of
    the generating set is contained in `𝔞` by construction. -/

    /-- **LEAF 3 — the genus is one** (sorry leaf, cut 2026-07-31 out of
    `exists_poleOrderValuation_of_affineComplement`; this is the ONLY one of the three that needs
    mathematics the tree does not have).
    
    * `∀ r ≠ 0, poleOrd r ≠ 1` is **genus `≥ 1`**: a function with a simple pole at `O` is a
      degree-one map `A → P¹`, hence an isomorphism, and `P¹` carries no abelian-scheme structure
      (an abelian scheme has translation-invariant, hence trivial, canonical bundle, so
      `2g - 2 = 0`).
    * `∃ x, poleOrd x = 2` and `∃ y, poleOrd y = 3` are **genus `≤ 1`**, i.e. Riemann's
      inequality `dim L(n[O]) ≥ n + 1 - g` read at `n = 2` and `n = 3`.
    
    Together with the valuation clauses proven in this file these pin the value semigroup of
    `poleOrd` to `⟨2, 3⟩ = ℕ ∖ {1}`, which is what
    `Fermat.PoleOrderFiltration.exists_deg_eq` consumes.
    
    **WHY THIS IS STATED ABOUT `poleOrd` AND NOT ABOUT AN ARBITRARY `deg`.**  It has to be.  The
    valuation clauses do not pin the function: `2 · poleOrd` satisfies every one of them, and
    also `hone`, while satisfying neither existential.  So a leaf quantified over all `deg` with
    those clauses would be FALSE, and the whole point of making `poleOrd` a `def` is that this
    leaf can name it.  (A scale-invariant substitute exists — "exactly one `n : ℕ` is not a value
    of `deg`", the Weierstrass gap theorem — but it is the same mathematics and a worse
    statement.)
    
    **WHAT WOULD REFUTE THE "MISSING" DIAGNOSIS**: a Riemann–Roch theorem, a genus, or a theory of
    divisors/linear systems on a curve, in `Fermat/`, `.lake/packages/mathlib` or `~/cs/FLT`.
    Absent from all three as of 2026-07-31.
    
    **NOT VACUOUS**: at the Weierstrass chart, `x` and `y` witness the two existentials and
    `2i + 3j = 1` has no solution in non-negative integers. -/

    /-- **`Pic⁰ ⟶ S` IS PROPER** (sorry leaf, cut 2026-07-31 out of
    `exists_relPicZeroSubfunctor`) — BLR 9.4, the second of the two classical
    chapters that leaf carried, and the one the valuative criterion for line bundles
    on a relative curve is for.
    
    The hypotheses are the conclusion of `exists_relPicIdentityComponent` verbatim,
    plus the curve and `Pic` hypotheses that leaf already had.  Nothing about open
    immersions is asked for or offered: the clauses below already pin `J` as `Pic⁰`,
    and the derivation is written out under FAITHFULNESS.
    
    **The intended argument** (BLR 9.4/4, and 8.4 for the finiteness inputs).
    `Pic_{X/S}` is smooth (`_hPsmooth`) and separated (`_hPsep`) over `S`, and
    `f_*𝒪 = 𝒪` universally (`_hpush`) is what makes its `T`-points the naive
    quotient `Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)` rather than an fppf sheafification, which is the form
    `hP` states.  Properness of the degree-zero part is then the valuative
    criterion: for a valuation ring `R` with fraction field `K` and a degree-zero
    class on `X_K`, the closure of the corresponding divisor in `X_R` is a divisor
    whose degree on the special fibre can be corrected to `0` by a multiple of the
    special fibre itself — `X_R ⟶ Spec R` being proper, smooth and with
    geometrically connected fibres, so its fibres are irreducible and the degree map
    is defined.  Uniqueness of the extension is separatedness.  Finite-type-ness,
    the other half of properness, is BLR 8.4/3 (`Pic` is locally of finite type,
    and `Pic⁰` is quasi-compact because it is a CONNECTED group scheme locally of
    finite type over a field on each fibre — SGA3 VI_A 2.4).
    
    **FAITHFULNESS — and this is the load-bearing check of the 2026-07-31 cut, not
    a formality.**  Splitting a conjunction `A ∧ B` into `A` and `A → B` is only
    faithfulness-neutral if `B` holds for EVERY witness of `A`.  Here `A` was
    weakened by deleting `IsProper`, so witnesses that the deleted conjunct used to
    exclude are now admitted, and the question is whether any of them fails
    properness.  None does, and here is why: the hypotheses force `J = Pic⁰`.
    
    1. `_hinclpre` and `_hinj` make `incl` a monomorphism of functors on `Over S`.
       By Yoneda (evaluate at `T = J`, `g = jstr`, on the tautological point) it is
       `(· ≫ ι)` for a unique `ι : J ⟶ P` over `S`, and `ι` is a monomorphism of
       schemes.
    2. `_hzero`, `_hadd`, `_hneg` make the image a SUBGROUP functor of `Pic` — the
       three clauses are exactly closure under the three operations, and each is an
       honest closure statement because `hP.inj` makes the point classifying a given
       sheaf unique (see the section heading before `exists_relPicIdentityComponent`).
    3. `_hJconn` says every geometric fibre `J_s̄` is a CONNECTED topological space,
       which in `Mathlib`'s `ConnectedSpace` includes NONEMPTY.  Together with 2 it
       places `J_s̄` inside the identity component of `Pic_s̄`, i.e. `J_s̄ ⊆ Pic⁰_s̄`.
       This is where the clause that replaced `IsProper` does its work: without it
       `J = P`, `incl = id` satisfies 1 and 2 and the Abel–Jacobi clause, and `Pic`
       is NOT proper — so `GeometricallyConnected jstr` is the hypothesis that makes
       this leaf true, and it may not be dropped.
    4. `_himg` puts the class of `𝒪(x − o)` in `J_s̄` for every point `x` of the
       fibre `X_s̄`.  Those classes GENERATE `Pic⁰_s̄` as a group (Riemann–Roch: every
       degree-zero class on a smooth projective connected curve of genus `g` is
       `𝒪(D − g·o)` for an effective `D` of degree `g`, hence a sum of `g` such
       differences), so with 2 we get `J_s̄ ⊇ Pic⁰_s̄` on points.
    5. A monomorphism of group schemes of finite type over a field is a closed
       immersion (SGA3 VI_B 1.4.2), and `J_s̄` is of finite type by the SGA3 VI_A 2.4
       remark above, so 3 + 4 give `J_s̄ = Pic⁰_s̄` as schemes, fibrewise, and `ι` is
       an isomorphism onto `Pic⁰`.  `Pic⁰ ⟶ S` is proper by BLR 9.4/4.
    
    So the leaf is TRUE for every witness of `exists_relPicIdentityComponent`, which
    is what the cut needed.
    
    **Which clauses are load-bearing, tested by deleting them one at a time.**
    
    * Drop `_hJconn` and it is FALSE, by `J = P`, `incl = id` as in 3 above: every
      other clause survives (`_himg` holds with `p := aj T g x`), and `Pic_{X/S}` is
      not proper over `S` — it is a disjoint union of the `Pic^d`, of which there
      are infinitely many.  This is the sharpest witness in the audit and the reason
      the connectedness clause is stated on the LEAF rather than derived.
    * Drop `_hinj` and it is FALSE: `J := Pic⁰ ⊔ 𝔸¹_S` with `incl` sending both
      copies into `Pic⁰`… fails `_hJconn`; the honest witness is
      `J := Pic⁰ ×_S 𝔸¹_S` with `incl` the first projection on points, which is
      smooth, has geometrically connected fibres, has image closed under the group
      law and containing the Abel–Jacobi image, and is not proper.  So injectivity
      is load-bearing too.
    * `_himg` is NOT load-bearing for this leaf, and the audit says so rather than
      claiming a witness it does not have: by 2 and 3 alone `J_s̄` is a connected
      subgroup functor of `Pic⁰_s̄`, `Pic⁰_s̄` is an abelian variety (the curve is
      smooth and proper), and a monomorphism from a smooth connected group scheme
      into an abelian variety is a closed immersion onto an abelian subvariety,
      hence proper.  The clause is nevertheless KEPT, for two reasons: it is
      supplied free by the sibling leaf, and it upgrades "`J` is *some* abelian
      subvariety of `Pic⁰`" to "`J` IS `Pic⁰`", which is what the name claims and
      what `exists_relPicZeroSubgroup`'s consumers read the result as.  Dropping a
      hypothesis strengthens a leaf, and this development has a standing record of
      restatements that composed into a false statement
      (`exists_artinDivisorNormIndex_le_ray_class`); a prover who finds it genuinely
      idle should delete it THEN, with a proof in hand.
    * The curve hypotheses `_hproper`, `_hsmooth`, `_hconn`, `o` and `_hpush` are
      all spent: smoothness and properness of the curve are what make `Pic⁰` an
      abelian scheme at all, geometric connectedness of the fibres is what makes the
      degree map well defined in the valuative criterion, the section `o` is what
      makes the naive quotient `Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)` the right functor (BLR 8.1/4), and
      `_hpush` is what `hP` needs in order to be about that quotient. -/

    Mazur's table is an ENDOMORPHISM `ψ` of `E_ℚ̄` with `ψ² = [−p]`.

    `isolatedCMJInvariants` verifies: on all five entries the `p`-isogenous curve has

    asserts exists — keeps it one by `IsIsogeny.comp`.  It must NOT be weakened to a
    bare `AddMonoidHom`, for the reason recorded on the parent: `X² + p` has a root
    in `M₂(Ẑ)`, so every curve carries an abstract `ψ` with `ψ² = [−p]`.

    /-- **THE COMPONENTS OF THE RIGIDIFIED MODULI SCHEME OVER `𝔽_p`, AND THAT THE DECK GROUP
    PERMUTES THEM TRANSITIVELY** (sorry leaf, opened 2026-07-31 as the single modular input of
    `isDomain_of_gamma0AtlasOver_zmod`, which moved below `coarseRing_algEquiv_zmod` and became
    a THEOREM the same day) — Deligne–Rapoport IV.5.5 / VI.6.7 together with the Weil-pairing
    determinant formula.
    
    `𝔐([Γ₀(N)], [Γ(n)])_{𝔽_p}` is a disjoint union of smooth affine curves, and `G = GL₂(ℤ/n)`
    permutes those components transitively.  Formally: `P.A` is REDUCED and nontrivial, and `G`
    acts transitively on `minimalPrimes P.A`.
    
    ## Why this is the whole of what was owed
    
    The old statement here was `IsDomain Γ(A.Y, ⊤)` and its docstring said the prover owed "that
    `B = Γ(Y, ⊤) = A^G` has no zero divisors — **NOT** that `A` is a domain", and then named the
    two ingredients:
    
    * each geometric component of `𝔐([Γ₀(N)], [Γ(n)])_{𝔽̄_p}` is irreducible — Deligne–Rapoport
      IV.5.5, and this is the genuine citation;
    * `det : GL₂(ℤ/n) → (ℤ/n)ˣ` is surjective and `e_n(gP, gQ) = e_n(P, Q)^{det g}`, so `G`
      permutes those components TRANSITIVELY even where Frobenius does not — which is what makes
      the invariants a domain although `A` is not.
    
    Both of those are statements about `P.A` and the action of `P.G` on it, and NEITHER mentions
    the coarse ring, the invariants, an atlas or a scheme.  The passage from them to
    `IsDomain Γ(A.Y, ⊤)` is not modular at all: it is
    `Algebra.IsInvariant.isDomain_of_transitive_minimalPrimes` in
    `Fermat/FLT/Mathlib/RingTheory/InvariantCoarseRing.lean` (PROVEN 2026-07-31, ~30 lines of
    prime avoidance) followed by `coarseRing_algEquiv_zmod`.  So the leaf count is unchanged,
    `1 → 1`, and what changed is that the invariant theory can never have to be got right again
    and the surviving statement is dispatchable at somebody who knows Deligne–Rapoport and
    nothing else about this file.
    
    ## MINIMAL PRIMES, NOT CONNECTED COMPONENTS
    
    The geometric sentence is "`G` is transitive on the connected components of `Spec P.A`", and
    for the Katz–Mazur model the two agree: `𝔐_{𝔽_p}` is SMOOTH, so its irreducible components
    are disjoint and are exactly its connected components.  Minimal primes are the right formal
    carrier all the same — they are what reducedness controls
    (`⋂ minimalPrimes = nilradical = 0`), they are what the invariant-theory lemma consumes, and
    they need no idempotent, no product decomposition and no topology to be constructed.  A
    prover following Deligne–Rapoport produces the component decomposition and reads the minimal
    primes off it; nothing is lost in the translation.
    
    ## Why `∃ P` and not `∀ P`
    
    Exactly as on `exists_gamma0GITPresentationOver_normalModuli_zmod` below, and for the same
    reason: `A := A₀ × A₀` with `G := G₀ × ZMod 2` acting by the factor swap has the same `B`,
    the same `str` and the same `classify`, so a `∀`-shaped statement would have to survive
    substitutions that the structure does not see.  (This particular substitution happens to
    PRESERVE transitivity — the swap is what does it — but that is luck, not an argument, and
    the `∃` costs nothing because `coarseRing_algEquiv_zmod` transports the conclusion, which is
    about `B`, to every atlas anyway.)
    
    ## Why `IsReduced P.A` is asserted here as well as on the normality leaf
    
    `exists_gamma0GITPresentationOver_normalModuli_zmod` below also concludes `IsReduced P.A`,
    so the two leaves overlap in one conjunct.  They cannot be merged, and the reason is

    invariant-theory lemma needs reducedness and transitivity **on the same `P`**, which is why
    this leaf carries both and does not import the first from its sibling.

      `Γ₀(0)`-datum forces its base to be empty (`isEmpty_of_gamma0Datum_zero`), so `P.A` is the

    * **`hpN : ¬ p ∣ N` is REQUIRED.**  At `p ∥ N` the Deligne–Rapoport model V.1.16 has the
      fibre of `X_0(N)` equal to two copies of `X_0(N/p)` crossing TRANSVERSALLY at the

    **This is a RE-CUT of `exists_cuspAboveDivisor_root`, not a weakening and not a

    with Koizumi's theorem (`L^{⊗n}` is projectively normal for `n ≥ 3`) — one classical
    package about `L` alone, saying nothing about the group law.  What it delivers:
    
    * `M` with `M ≅ L^{⊗3}`, invertible, and a finite family `s : Fin dim → Γ(M, ⊤)`;
    * `φ`, a trivialization of `P^*M` at each rational point.  `P^*M` is invertible on
      `Spec ℚ` and `Pic(Spec ℚ) = 0`, so this is free; it is handed over rather than
      constructed because constructing it needs "an invertible sheaf on a one-point scheme
      is globally trivial", which is true and is not in the pin;
    * BASE-POINT FREENESS, `∀ z, ∃ i, NonvanishingAt M (s i) z`.  Note this is stated on
      `J`, about the sheaf — no coordinates — and `ptSectionValue_ne_zero_iff` converts it
      into `CubeModel.coords_ne_zero`;
    * SEPARATION OF RATIONAL POINTS, in the coordinate-free form "some `2 × 2` minor of the
      two coordinate vectors is nonzero".  For nonzero vectors over a field, all minors
      vanishing IS proportionality, so this says exactly that the map to `ℙ^{dim−1}(ℚ)`
      induced by `s` is injective, which is that a closed immersion is a monomorphism;
    * `SpansSquare`, projective normality — see its docstring for why the cut is FALSE
      without it.

    *True.*  Every clause is a consequence of `L^{⊗3}` being very ample and projectively
    normal on the abelian variety `A = J`.  Base-point freeness and injectivity on
    `ℚ`-points are properties of a closed immersion `φ_{L³} : A ↪ ℙ^{dim−1}`; the minor
    form of injectivity needs the coordinate vectors to be nonzero, which base-point
    freeness supplies, and then "non-proportional ⟺ some minor ≠ 0" is linear algebra over
    a field.
    
    *Not vacuous.*  `dim = 0` is excluded by base-point freeness as soon as `J` is nonempty
    (there is then no `i` at all), and constant `coords` are excluded by separation as soon
    as `A(ℚ)` has two elements.  So this leaf cannot be discharged by a degenerate system,
    which is precisely the failure mode `CubeModel`'s corrected non-vacuity note records
    for `dim = 1`.
    
    *Not stronger than the geometry supplies.*  Nothing here mentions the cube, and the
    hypotheses are only `hinv` and `hamp` — symmetry and normalization are NOT used, and
    adding them would record hypotheses this half does not read.  `ab` is kept because the
    constant `3` is an abelian-variety statement: for a general proper scheme only "some
    power" is very ample. -/

    /-- **THE FORMS HALF: the theorem of the cube, read through a projectively normal very
    ample system, is a family of quadratic forms in the Segre variables** (sorry leaf, cut
    2026-07-31 out of `nonempty_cubeModel_of_isAmpleSheaf_cube` below).
    
    Given the system `(M, s, φ)` that `exists_veryAmpleSystem_of_isAmpleSheaf` produces,
    this manufactures every remaining field of `CubeModel`:
    
    * `cube` / `cube_eval` from `hcube`.  `HasCubeIso` is multiplicative in `L`, so
      `σ^*L ⊗ δ^*L ≅ p₁^*L^{⊗2} ⊗ p₂^*L^{⊗2}` gives the same identity for `M ≅ L^{⊗3}`.
      Under it, `σ^* s_k ⊗ δ^* s_l` is a global section of
      `p₁^*M^{⊗2} ⊗ p₂^*M^{⊗2}`, which Künneth identifies with
      `Γ(M^{⊗2}, ⊤) ⊗ Γ(M^{⊗2}, ⊤)`, and `hspan` writes each factor as a quadratic form in
      the `s_i` — bidegree `(2,2)`, i.e. degree `2` in the Segre variables;
    * `rel` / `rel_eval`: `J ×_ℚ J` is projective, so the Segre image is closed and its
      homogeneous ideal is finitely generated (Hilbert basis);
    * `cube_nonvanishing`: `(P, Q) ↦ (P + Q, P − Q)` is `⟨σ, δ⟩`, a morphism defined
      everywhere, so over `ℚ̄` the forms have no common zero on the cone over the Segre
      image apart from the origin.
    
    **THE BLOCKER IS KÜNNETH, NOT AMPLENESS.**  A sweep on 2026-07-31 found
    `grep -rn 'IsVeryAmple\|VeryAmple\|Kunneth\|Künneth'` empty across
    `.lake/packages/mathlib` and `~/cs/FLT` at this pin, so both classical inputs must be
    built inside `Fermat/`.  Of the two, very ampleness is consumed only by the OTHER half;
    what this one needs is the identification
    `Γ(p₁^*N ⊗ p₂^*N', ⊤) ≅ Γ(N, ⊤) ⊗ Γ(N', ⊤)` on a product of proper `ℚ`-schemes.  A
    prover should aim there first.
    
    **FAITHFULNESS AUDIT** (fresh; this leaf did not exist before today).
    
    *True.*  Mumford §6; Hindry–Silverman *Diophantine Geometry* B.5.1; Silverman *AEC*
    VIII.6.2 in the elliptic case.
    
    *The dependence on `φ` is harmless, and this is the clause that could have made the
    leaf false.*  `cube_eval` demands ONE scalar `c` valid for all `k` simultaneously.
    Replacing `φ (P+Q)` by `α · φ (P+Q)` and `φ (P−Q)` by `β · φ (P−Q)` multiplies the whole
    right-hand side by `α β`, uniformly in `k`, and the left-hand side by the corresponding
    scalars at `P` and `Q` raised to bidegree `(2,2)` — again uniformly.  So the truth of
    the statement does not depend on WHICH trivializations the embedding half handed over,
    which is what lets `φ` be a hypothesis instead of a construction.
    
    *`hsym` and `hzero` are the two a careless prover would drop.*  `hsym` is what makes the
    cube's right-hand side `p₁^*L^{⊗2} ⊗ p₂^*L^{⊗2}` rather than
    `p₁^*(L ⊗ [−1]^*L) ⊗ p₂^*(L ⊗ [−1]^*L)`; `hzero` normalizes the scalar `c`.
    
    *Not stronger than the geometry supplies.*  `hamp` is deliberately ABSENT: ampleness is
    consumed entirely by the embedding half, and what survives into the forms is the
    spanning clause, which is the part of it this half actually reads. -/

    /-- **DELIGNE IN WEIGHT TWO, READ ON THE HECKE OPERATOR** (sorry leaf, cut
    2026-07-31 out of `realCoeff_norm_le_of_isWeightTwoEigenform`) — the single
    archimedean input of this whole cluster, stated at the good primes in the
    vocabulary of this file's own Eichler–Shimura machinery.
    
    *Every eigenvalue of `T_ℓ` on `S₂(Γ₀(N))` at `ℓ ∤ N` is the trace of a pair of
    Weil numbers of weight one.*
    
    ### Why it is TRUE
    
    Eichler–Shimura: the `2g` eigenvalues of Frobenius on `H¹(X_0(N)_{𝔽̄_ℓ})` pair
    up as `αᵢ, βᵢ` with `αᵢ + βᵢ = aᵢ` and `αᵢ βᵢ = ℓ`, the `aᵢ` being the
    eigenvalues of `T_ℓ`; Weil's Riemann hypothesis for the curve `X_0(N)_{𝔽_ℓ}`
    (which has good reduction exactly because `ℓ ∤ N`) gives `|αᵢ| = |βᵢ| = √ℓ`.
    The eigenvalue of an oldform is that of the newform it comes from, at a level
    `M₀ ∣ N` still prime to `ℓ`, so nothing is lost by quantifying over the FULL
    cuspidal space rather than over newforms.
    
    ### The route inside THIS FILE, and the one statement it is missing
    
    Everything below already exists here:
    
    1. `exists_x0Compactification_finiteField N ℓ` — the curve `X_0(N)_{𝔽_ℓ}`;
    2. `exists_isWeilEigenvalues ℓ strX` — its Frobenius eigenvalue multiset `α`,
       pinned by the point counts over every finite extension;
    3. `exists_isCharRootMultiset (heckeOp N ℓ)` — the root multiset `a` of the
       characteristic polynomial of `T_ℓ`, unconditionally;
    4. `isEichlerShimuraTransform_x0 N ℓ … hα ha` — `IsEichlerShimuraTransform ℓ a α`,
       i.e. `α` is a union of pairs summing through `a` with each product `ℓ`,
       possibly together with entries equal to `0`.
    
    The ONLY missing input is **PURITY**:
    
    > for `strX : X ⟶ SpecF ℓ` proper, smooth of relative dimension `1` and
    > geometrically connected, and `IsWeilEigenvalues ℓ strX α`, every `z ∈ α` with
    > `z ≠ 0` has `‖z‖ = Real.sqrt ℓ`.
    
    That is Weil's theorem, it mentions no modular curve, and it is stated exactly
    where `IsWeilEigenvalues` is defined.  It is faithful in that shape because
    `IsWeilEigenvalues` pins `α` only UP TO ENTRIES EQUAL TO ZERO
    (`pow_sum_eq_of_isWeilEigenvalues`), so the `z ≠ 0` guard is required rather
    than defensive; and the entries this leaf consumes are automatically nonzero,
    their product being `ℓ ≠ 0`.  **Check the emptiness convention before writing
    it**: the section docstring on `IsWeilEigenvalues` observes that for an EMPTY
    `X` the counts force `α = {1, ℓ}`, which violates purity — so purity needs
    whatever hypothesis excludes the empty scheme (`GeometricallyConnected` does, if
    it is `ConnectedSpace`-based; otherwise add nonemptiness explicitly).
    
    ### Why this leaf is stated here and not proven there
    
    Declaration order — see the section docstring immediately above.  All four
    ingredients live 10 000 lines below this line, and neither block can move past
    the other, so a prover must first SPLIT this module.  Two further things that
    prover will need, and that are not obstacles to the STATEMENT:
    
    * `cuspForm_finiteDimensional` (in `Modularity/Interface.lean`, downstream) — an
      eigenvalue is a root of the characteristic polynomial only in finite
      dimension, and `IsCharRootMultiset` is deliberately stated without it (its
      junk value is the empty multiset).  Hoisting it is the same class of move as
      the one recorded on `heckeOp_smul_of_isWeightTwoEigenform` above;
    * nothing else.  In particular NO Petersson theory: the reality of `a_p`, which
      the old packaging obtained from self-adjointness of `T_p`, falls out of
      `α β = ℓ` together with `‖α‖ = √ℓ` — see `exists_real_of_weilPair` below.
    
    ### Reconnaissance (PARI/GP, 2026-07-28 — untrusted searcher)
    
    For every level `M ≤ 60` with `S₂(Γ₀(M)) ≠ 0` and every prime `q ≤ 40`, the
    matrix of `T_q` (resp. `U_q` when `q ∣ M`) on the FULL cuspidal space was formed
    and its characteristic polynomial's complex roots examined: at `q ∤ M` all roots
    are REAL with `|a_q| ≤ 2√q`; at `q ∣ M` all roots have `|a_q| ≤ √q`.  **540
    matrices, zero violations.**  The first column is this leaf (the reality it
    observes is the corollary below, not an extra assumption); the second is
    `norm_coeff_le_sqrt_of_dvd_level`.
    
    ### Axes searched, and why each dies
    
    * **The coefficient recursions alone.**  `hecke`/`atkin` constrain only the
      RELATIONS among the `a_n`, never their size.  The level-`0` counterexample
      recorded on `stabilizationRoot_ne_natCast` below is built entirely inside
      those recursions, so no proof using only them can exist.
    * **Radius of convergence.**  `qExpansionSummable` gives
      `limsup ‖a_n‖^{1/n} ≤ 1`, but along the sparse sequence `n = p^k` that is
      vacuous: `‖a_p‖^{k/p^k} → 1` whatever `‖a_p‖` is.
    * **Hecke's trivial bound**, including mathlib's new
      `CuspFormClass.qExpansion_isBigO` (`Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Bounds.lean`):
      `a_n = O(n)` in weight two, hence `‖a_p‖ ≤ p + 1` — one epsilon short of what
      `stabilizationRoot_ne_natCast` needs (`‖b_p‖ ≠ p + 1`), and `IsBigO` carries
      an UNSPECIFIED constant while `norm_coeff_le_two_mul_self` needs the explicit
      `2`.  The trivial bound is attained by the weight-two Eisenstein series, so
      the strictness wanted is exactly cuspidality, quantitatively.  It does not
      help the reality clause either, which is orthogonal to every size estimate.
    * **The `EichlerShimuraPackage` of `Modularity/Interface.lean`.**  It does
      supply `Frob_q² − T_q Frob_q + q = 0`, i.e. `α + β = a_q`, `α β = q` — but
      `Interface.lean` IMPORTS this file, and more decisively its coefficients live
      in `AlgebraicClosure ℚ_p` and it asserts nothing archimedean.  What turns that
      characteristic polynomial into a bound is purity, which is this leaf. -/

    /-- **RELATIVE RIEMANN–ROCH: fppf-locally, a degree-zero class twisted by `d·[o]` is
    EFFECTIVE and splits into `d` sections** (sorry leaf, cut 2026-07-31 out of
    `exists_flatSurj_ajListSum`, which is now PROVEN over it and over
    `relPicEquiv_sheaf_listSum_aj` above).
    
    This is `Sym^d C ↠ Pic^d` — **without needing `Sym^d` to be constructed** — and it
    mentions no group law, no `aj` and no `inj`.  Let `L := P.sheaf p` be the invertible
    sheaf on `C_T` classified by `p`, and put `d := max (2g − 1) 1` for `g` the (locally
    constant) genus of `f` on the image of `T`.  Then `L(d·o)` has fibre degree
    `d ≥ 2g − 1`, so `R¹π_* = 0`, `π_*L(d·o)` is locally free of rank `d − g + 1 > 0`,
    and the projective bundle `ℙ(π_*L(d·o)) ⟶ T` is smooth surjective; its tautological
    section cuts a relative effective divisor of degree `d` in the class.  Splitting that
    divisor into `d` individual sections costs one further étale cover (a smooth
    surjection has sections étale-locally, Stacks 054F, applied on the open locus where
    the divisor is étale over the base — nonempty in every fibre once the residue field
    is enlarged).  A composite of a smooth surjection and an étale surjection is flat and
    surjective, which is all the conclusion asks for.  Literature: Milne, *Jacobian
    Varieties* §§2–5; BLR *Néron Models* 9.4; ACGH ch. IV for `Sym^d C ⟶ Pic^d`.
    
    `QuasiCompact h` comes free from the same objects: the projective bundle is proper
    hence quasi-compact, the étale cover splitting the divisor is finite over the base,
    and a composite of quasi-compact morphisms is quasi-compact.  It is in the conclusion
    because `exists_albaneseFactorisation` descends a MORPHISM along `h` and therefore
    needs `EffectiveEpi h` (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean`), not merely
    `Epi h`.
    
    **`[CompactSpace T]` IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE STATEMENT IS FALSE WITHOUT IT.**  The
    list `l` has ONE length, and `d` above is bounded only because the genus takes
    finitely many values on a quasi-compact `T`.  Witness: let `S = ⨆_{g ≥ 2} Spec ℚ` and
    `C = ⨆_{g ≥ 2} C_g` with `C_g` a smooth projective curve over `ℚ` of genus `g`, so
    `f` is a smooth proper relative curve with geometrically connected fibres, and take
    `T = J`, `p` the universal point.  For any list of length `n` the composite `h`
    factors set-theoretically through the image of the `n`-fold sum map `C^n ⟶ J`, whose
    restriction over the genus-`g` component has dimension at most `n`; so on any
    component with `g > n` that image is a proper closed subscheme of the `g`-dimensional
    `J_g` and `h` cannot be surjective.
    
    **FALSITY AUDIT — WHY `P` STAYS IN THE STATEMENT, i.e. why this is not stated for an
    arbitrary invertible `L`.**  The obvious `P`-free generalisation
    
    > for every invertible `L` on `C_T` there are `T' ⟶ T` flat surjective quasi-compact
    > and `l` with `φ^*L ⊗ ⊗ᵢ𝒪(−yᵢ) ∼ 𝒪(−o)^{⊗ l.length}`
    
    is **FALSE**, and the counterexample is one line of degree bookkeeping.  Take
    `S = T = Spec k`, `C/k` a smooth projective curve, and `L` of degree `m ≠ 0`.  A
    cover `T' ⟶ T` is a nonempty `k`-scheme; comparing fibre degrees at any point of `T'`
    (the twist `π^*N` in `RelPicEquiv` has fibre degree `0`, being pulled back from the
    base) gives `m − l.length = − l.length`, i.e. `m = 0`.  So the `P`-free statement
    holds precisely for `L` of relative degree `0`.
    
    `P.sheaf p` HAS relative degree `0`, and that is a consequence of the structure
    rather than an extra hypothesis: `deg ∘ P.sheaf` is a locally constant `ℤ`-valued
    function on `T`, additive by `sheaf_add`, zero at the origin by `sheaf_zero`, and
    zero on the Abel–Jacobi image by `aj_spec` (`1 − 1 = 0`); since `jf` has
    geometrically connected fibres it is therefore identically `0`.  There is no degree
    theory at this pin to say any of that formally, which is exactly why the leaf is
    stated for `P.sheaf p` and not for a general `L` — the hypothesis "degree zero" is
    not expressible here, and `P` is the only thing in scope that carries it.
    
    The same audit explains why the two occurrences of `l.length` in the conclusion may
    not be relaxed to two independent numbers.  With an independent `n` the statement is
    true for arbitrary `L` (`𝒪(D' − D)` with `#D' − #D = deg L`), but it no longer
    matches `relPicEquiv_sheaf_listSum_aj`, whose two lengths are equal by construction,
    and the assembly below cannot close — one would have to prove `deg L = 0` on the way,
    which is the theory that does not exist.
    
    **NOT VACUOUS.**  `l = []` forces `P.sheaf p ∼ 𝒪`, hence `p = 0` by `inj` and

    /-- **ABEL'S THEOREM, with `Pic⁰` REMOVED FROM THE STATEMENT** (sorry leaf, cut
    2026-07-31 out of `IsRelPicZeroOf.listSum_map_eq_of_listSum_aj_eq`, which is now
    PROVEN over it and over `relPicEquiv_divisor_of_listSum_aj_eq` above): the divisor
    map `Σ nᵢ[yᵢ] ↦ Σ nᵢ c(yᵢ)` into an abelian scheme depends only on the relative
    LINEAR EQUIVALENCE class of the divisor.
    
    Equivalently: `Sym^d C ⟶ A` factors through `Pic^d_{C/S}`.  This is the classical
    Abel theorem for a map to an abelian variety, proved by the theorem of the cube /
    the seesaw theorem (Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* §§6 and 11; Milne, *Jacobian
    Varieties* §§2–6; BLR *Néron Models* 8.4).
    
    **WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT CUT.**  The node it replaces took its hypothesis in the
    vocabulary of `IsRelPicZeroOf` — "the two lists have equal `aj`-sums" — which is a
    statement about a representing object for `Pic⁰` that a classical proof never
    mentions.  Here the hypothesis is a linear equivalence of two EFFECTIVE divisors on
    the curve, and the conclusion is about `c` alone.  Nothing in the statement mentions
    `J`, `ab`, `aj`, `sheaf` or `inj`; the only project vocabulary left is
    `RelPicEquiv`, which is `Pic(C_T)/Pic(T)` and is unavoidable — the relative Picard
    group is what "linearly equivalent over a base" MEANS.
    
    **FAITHFULNESS.  `hnat` and `hpt` are both load-bearing, with the same two witnesses
    as on the node this replaces**, transported through
    `relPicEquiv_divisor_of_listSum_aj_eq`, which is an implication and so carries any
    counterexample to the hypothesis side unchanged:
    
    * without `hnat`, take `l = [o_T]`, `l' = []`: the divisors `1·[o] + 0` and
      `0·[o] + [o_T]` are equal, hence certainly equivalent, and the conclusion forces
      `c g o_T = 0`.  A non-natural `c` vanishing at `(𝟙 S, o)` and not at some other
      test object violates exactly that;
    * without `hpt`, the constant family `c g x := τ|_T` for a nonzero `τ` is natural
      and gives `τ_T ≠ 0 = 0` on the same pair.
    
    **THE TWIST `π^*N` IN `RelPicEquiv` IS NOT A WEAKENING OF THE HYPOTHESIS, and this
    is the one check a prover must not skip.**  `RelPicEquiv` allows the two divisor
    sheaves to differ by a sheaf pulled back from `T`, not merely by a principal
    divisor.  That is still enough: a `π^*N` restricts to `𝒪` on every fibre, so the
    difference of the two divisors is fibrewise principal, which is precisely the
    hypothesis of the relative Abel theorem — and it is the RIGHT hypothesis, because
    `Sym^d C ⟶ A` factors through the RELATIVE Picard functor `Pic(C_T)/Pic(T)`, not
    through `Pic(C_T)`.  Weakening `RelPicEquiv` to plain isomorphism here would make
    the leaf strictly weaker than its consumer needs, since
    `relPicEquiv_divisor_of_listSum_aj_eq` can only ever produce a `RelPicEquiv`.
    
    **NOT VACUOUS.**  `l = l'` makes the hypothesis an identity and the conclusion an
    identity; the content is at `l ≠ l'`, and such pairs exist as soon as the curve has
    genus `≥ 1`, because then `Sym^d C ⟶ Pic^d` has positive-dimensional fibres for

    /-- **GOOD REDUCTION ON A GIT MODEL: some atlas over `ℤ_(ℓ)` has the
    categorical-quotient property at the CLOSED POINT** (sorry leaf, opened
    2026-07-31 — Katz–Mazur (8.1.6), Deligne–Rapoport, Igusa).
    
    This is the special-fibre twin of `exists_gamma0AtlasOver_bcQuotient_of_field`,
    and it replaces `universal_classifyPullback_special`, which is PROVEN over it
    (through `bcUniversal_specLocSpecial` just below).  The leaf count is unchanged;
    what changed is that the statement is now attackable on a model of one's own
    choosing.
    
    ## What it says, unfolded
    
    `Gamma0AtlasOver.BcQuotient q` at `q = SpecLoc.special toF` asks that a morphism
    out of `𝔐 ×_{ℤ_(ℓ)} 𝔽_ℓ` over `𝔽_ℓ`, which does not separate two rigidifications
    of one datum lying over one base point, factor uniquely — over `𝔽_ℓ` — through
    the classifying map of the base-changed universal family.  On a GIT model, where
    `𝔐 = Spec A` and `Y = Spec (A^G)`, that is the assertion
    
        Spec (A^G ⊗_R 𝔽_ℓ)  is the categorical quotient of  Spec (A ⊗_R 𝔽_ℓ)  by  G
    
    in `𝔽_ℓ`-schemes.  Everything ELSE about this base change is already formal:
    `Gamma0AtlasOver.baseChange` builds seven of the eight atlas fields at an
    ARBITRARY base morphism, out of `exists_gamma0Datum_baseChange` and
    `IsBaseChangeOf.cancel`, and `bcQuotient_of_bcUniversal` /
    `bcUniversal_of_bcQuotient` make the quotient and initiality forms equivalent at
    an arbitrary `q`.  So a prover owes exactly the displayed line and nothing else.
    
    ## Why `A` is a hypothesis, and why the conclusion is existential
    
    Both for the reason recorded on `exists_gamma0AtlasOver_bcQuotient_of_field`.
    Without `A` the statement would also assert `Nonempty (Gamma0AtlasOver N (SpecLoc R))`,
    which is a DIFFERENT theorem (`nonempty_gamma0AtlasOver_specLoc`, already proven
    for `0 < N`) and does not belong here.  And a lazy witness `A'` cannot weaken the
    consumer: `bcUniversal_transport` derives the conclusion for the GIVEN atlas from
    whatever `A'` is supplied, through the canonical classify-compatible isomorphism
    of coarse spaces, so no choice of model can make the statement cheaper than it is.
    
    ## Why nothing formal reaches it
    
    `bcUniversal_of_flat` — (8.1.6)(2) at a flat extension of scalars — is what closes
    the generic side (`bcUniversal_specLocGeneric` above) and the field side
    (`bcUniversal_of_field`).  It does NOT reach the closed point, for two independent
    reasons: `ℤ_(ℓ) → 𝔽_ℓ` is not flat, and `ℓ` need not be prime to `#G`
    (`#GL₂(ℤ/3) = 48`, so `ℓ = 2` divides it already at the auxiliary level that
    `exists_gamma0Rigidification_specF` chooses).  So "invariants commute with base
    change" fails here for FORMAL reasons, and Katz–Mazur Remark (8.1.7)'s
    counterexamples at `p = 2, 3` are about precisely this base change.  The content
    has to come from the geometry of the moduli problem over `ℤ[1/N]` — flatness of
    `𝔐` over the base, and reducedness of the special fibre — and not from invariant
    theory alone.  Do not expect a `specInvariants_universal`-shaped proof: that is
    what `Gamma0GITPresentationOver.bcQuot_universal_of_field` is on the field side,
    and its argument is exactly the one that breaks here.
    
    ## DO NOT attack it through the `𝔽_ℓ`-side coarse space — that is CIRCULAR
    
    `exists_isCoarseModuliY0_specInvariants` does give a coarse moduli space
    `Spec (A^G)` for `Γ₀(N)/𝔽_ℓ`, and coarse spaces are pinned up to unique
    isomorphism by initiality — so "compare the special fibre with `Spec (A^G)`" IS
    `isIso_specialFibreInvariantsQuotient`, which is PROVEN over this leaf's consumer.
    `exists_specialFibreInvariantsIso`, `exists_gamma0GITPresentationData_pullbackSpecial`,
    `exists_gamma0AtlasData_pullbackSpecial` and `nonempty_isCoarseModuliY0_pullbackSpecial`
    are all downstream of it for the same reason, so none of them is an input here.
    The `𝔽_ℓ`-side objects that ARE legitimate inputs are the ones built directly in
    characteristic `ℓ` and independent of the integral model:
    `exists_gamma0Rigidification_specF` and `nonempty_gamma0CurveAtlasOver_zmod`.
    
    ## Faithfulness
    
    `_hℓN` is load-bearing for TRUTH, not merely carried: at `ℓ ∣ N` the special fibre
    of `Y_0(N)_{ℤ_(ℓ)}` is the Deligne–Rapoport crossing of two Igusa components and
    is not the coarse space of `Γ₀(N)/𝔽_ℓ` at all, so the quotient property fails.
    `_hbase` is what makes `SpecLoc.special toF` the honest closed point rather than

    every neighbour in this cluster.  Note `_hℓN` also forces `0 < N` outright
    (`ℓ ∣ 0` for every `ℓ`), so the degenerate level cannot arise under these
    hypotheses and no `N = 0` branch is owed anywhere below. -/

    single sharpest way to see why the integral model is a citation and the rational
    one is not.

    up to isomorphism over the base (see the subsection comment: integral + normal +

    That is what makes a statement about an ARBITRARY model true rather than a
    statement about a chosen one, and it is the assumption a successor should check
    first if the leaf resists.

    and was left undone only for budget: `XZ` is flat over the DVR base (integral,
    dominating a Dedekind base ⟹ torsion-free ⟹ flat), so by the fibrewise criterion
    smoothness reduces to smoothness of the SPECIAL FIBRE `XZ ×_{ℤ_(ℓ)} 𝔽_ℓ` over
    `𝔽_ℓ`, which is Igusa's theorem proper, plus smoothness of the generic fibre,
    which is `_hX`-free general curve theory over `ℚ` and already available in this
    file.  Splitting there converts one citation into one citation and two proofs. -/

    own vocabulary exactly what the classical argument starts from: an isogeny
    `ψ : E ⟶ E` with `ker ψ = C` cyclic of order `169`, a dual `ψ̂` with

    `ker_map` and `ker_dual` give `ker ψ = C = ker ψ̂`, and `dual_map` gives
    `ψ̂ψ = [169]`.  Equal kernels force `ψ̂ = uψ` for a unit `u` of `End(E)`, and
    then `uψ² = ψ̂ψ = [169]`.
    
    **Step 2 — the loophole, and why it is closed by CYCLICITY rather than by a
    class number.**  `u = 1` gives `ψ² = 169`, so `ψ = ±13 ∈ ℤ` and
    `ker ψ = E[13] ≅ (ℤ/13)²`, which is NOT cyclic of order `169`; the extra
    units `u = ±i` exist only for `j = 1728` and force `tr(ψ)² = 2 · 169 = 338`,
    not a square (`18² = 324 < 338 < 361 = 19²`); `u` a primitive sixth root
    exists only for `j = 0` and forces `tr(ψ)² = 169`, i.e. `ψ = ±13ζ` with
    `ker ψ = E[13]` again.  So `u = −1` and `tr ψ = 0`, i.e. **`ψ² = −169`,
    `ψ = ±13i`** — there is no other square root of `−169` in any imaginary
    quadratic field.  The order `O = End(E)` therefore contains `ℤ[13i]`, and
    the only orders of `ℚ(i)` doing so are `ℤ[13i]` and the maximal order
    `ℤ[i]`.  The maximal order is excluded by the LEVEL STRUCTURE, before any

    /-- **THE NORM-ENDOMORPHISM PAIR OF A SURJECTION** (sorry leaf, new
    2026-07-31) — the whole of what is left of
    `exists_finiteKernelComplement_of_surjective_isAdditiveOn` below, which is
    PROVEN over it.
    
    **WHAT IT ASKS FOR.**  Two endomorphisms `c, d` of `J` over `ℚ`, with `c`
    additive, such that
    
    * `c ≫ d = 0` — the image of `c` lies in `ker d`;
    * `c ≫ u` is surjective — the image of `c` still maps ONTO `A`;
    * `ker d ∩ ker u` is a FINITE `ℚ`-scheme (`IsFinite` of the structure morphism
      of `ker (ker d ↪ J ≫ u)`).
    
    `d` is not required to be additive and no idempotence equation is imposed:
    those are properties of the intended construction, not of what the consumer
    spends.  The three clauses above are exactly what the proof below consumes,
    and nothing else.
    
    **WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT CUT.**  The leaf below had to produce an abelian
    scheme `B` and a map INTO `J` — i.e. an abelian SUBvariety — which is why the
    "image, not quotient" substitution that closed `exists_involutionSignSplitting`
    does not apply to it (that structure only ever needs maps OUT of `A`).  This
    leaf produces no scheme at all: it is a statement about `End(J)` and two
    kernels.  `B` is then `Im c`, delivered by
    `exists_addSurjectiveAbelianImage_of_isAdditiveOn_aux` above, and every
    scheme-theoretic step below — surjectivity, the factorisation through `ker d`,
    and the finiteness transport — is proven.
    
    TRUE and classical (Mumford, *Abelian Varieties* §19 Thm 1; Milne, *Abelian
    Varieties* I.12.1).  Over a field of characteristic `0` put `Y := (ker u)⁰`,
    fix a polarisation `λ` of `J`, and let `N_Y ∈ End J` be the NORM
    ENDOMORPHISM of `Y` — `N_Y = ι_Y ∘ ψ ∘ ι_Y^∨ ∘ λ` with `ψ` the
    `deg λ|_Y`-multiple inverse of `λ|_Y`, so that `N_Y ∘ N_Y = n · N_Y` for an
    `n ≥ 1` and `Im N_Y = Y`.  Take
    
        d := N_Y,        c := [n] − N_Y.
    
    Then `c ≫ d = n·N_Y − N_Y² = 0`; `c ≫ u = [n] ∘ u` because `N_Y` factors
    through `Y ⊆ ker u`, and `[n]` is surjective (`surjective_mulByNat`), so
    `c ≫ u` is surjective; and `ker N_Y ∩ ker u` is killed by `n·m`, where `m` is
    the order of the finite group `(ker u)/Y` — for `x` in it, `m·x ∈ Y ∩ ker N_Y`,
    and `N_Y` acts on `Y` as `[n]` — hence finite.
    
    **DEGENERATE CASES CHECK OUT.**  If `u` is already an isogeny then `Y = 0`,
    `N_Y = 0`, and the pair is `c = 𝟙`, `d = 0`: the last clause reads "`ker u` is
    finite", which is what "isogeny" means.  If `A` is a point then `Y = J`,
    `N_Y = [n]`, `c = 0` and `d = [n]`: `c ≫ u` is the structure morphism of a
    nonempty scheme onto `Spec ℚ`, surjective, and `ker [n] ∩ ker u = J[n]` is
    finite.
    
    **FALSITY AUDIT — NOT JUNK-SATISFIABLE, and the finiteness clause is where
    all the content sits.**  This is a FIRST audit: the statement is new and
    inherits none.
    
    * `c := 𝟙`, `d := 0` (the zero endomorphism `jstr ≫ zeroSection`) satisfies
      `c ≫ d = 0` and `Surjective (c ≫ u) = Surjective u`, and FAILS the third
      clause except when `u` is itself an isogeny: `ker 0 = J`, so the clause
      becomes `IsFinite (ker u ⟶ Spec ℚ)`.  `J = A × A'` with `u = pr₁` and
      `A' ≠ 0` refutes it.
    * `c := 0` fails `Surjective (c ≫ u)` unless `A` is a point: the image of
      `jstr ≫ abA.zeroSection` is the single point `e ∈ A`.
    * `d := 𝟙` forces `c = c ≫ 𝟙 = 0`, i.e. the previous case.
    
    **`_hsurj` MAY NOT BE DROPPED.**  Witness `J := E`, `A := E × E`,
    `u := (𝟙, 0)` — the parent's witness, and it kills this statement for the same
    reason: `c ≫ u : E ⟶ E × E` factors through a curve, so it is never surjective
    onto a surface, whatever `c` is.
    
    **`_hadd` IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR TRUTH** (same as the parent, and by the same
    rigidity argument: every morphism of abelian varieties is a translate

       fibre of `f` over a `K`-point `c` is the zero divisor of `f − c`, of degree

    **What the hypotheses say, in classical language.**  `IsNIsogenyPair N d d` gives
    an isogeny `φ : E ⟶ E` with `ker φ = C` together with a `ψ : E ⟶ E` with
    `ker ψ = C` and `ψφ = φψ = [N]`.  Since `ψ` is the dual, `ker ψ = φ(E[N])`, so the
    two kernel clauses read `φ(E[N]) = C = ker φ` — which is exactly
    `(E/C, E[N]/C) ≅ (E, C)`, i.e. `(E, C)` is a fixed point of `w_N`.  `hd` says the
    moduli point of `d` over `ℚ̄` is the base change of the `ℚ`-point `y`, i.e. the

    TRUE, by the CM count.  Composing `E → E/C ≅ E` gives an endomorphism of `E` of
    degree `N` with cyclic kernel, so `E` has complex multiplication by an order
    containing `√−N`; the possible orders are those between `ℤ[√−N]` (discriminant
    `−4N`) and the maximal order of `ℚ(√−N)`, and the conductor of `ℤ[√−N]` is `1`
    unless `N ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, when it is `2` and the maximal order (discriminant `−N`)
    also occurs.  A CM point of discriminant `D` is defined over the ring class field
    of that order, on which `Cl(𝒪_D)` acts simply transitively, so a `ℚ`-RATIONAL one
    forces `h(D) = 1`.  Recomputed in PARI/GP 2.17.4 on 2026-07-31
    (`quadclassunit(D).no`):
    
    | `N` | `N mod 4` | discriminants that occur | class numbers |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `65` | `1` | `−260` | `h(−260) = 8` |
    | `91` | `3` | `−364`, `−91` | `h(−364) = 6`, `h(−91) = 2` |
    
    All are `> 1`, and `91 ≡ 3 (mod 4)` is why the second row carries two — that
    extra family is absent at `169 ≡ 1` and is the one difference from the `169`

    conductor-`2` order inside the field of discriminant `−91`.)

    `hN : 4 ≤ N` is **load-bearing for TRUTH**, and this is the one place in the
    tower where that differs from the merged node.  At `N ≤ 3` the problem is not
    rigid, so no fine moduli scheme exists and `Gamma1ModuliScheme N (Spec K)` is
    UNINHABITED: at `N = 3` take `K = ℚ̄` and `E : y² = x³ + 1` (so `j = 0`), whose
    automorphism `ζ : (x, y) ↦ (ωx, y)` of order `3` fixes the point `(0, 1)` of
    exact order `3`.  A nontrivial automorphism of `(E, P)` makes the classifying
    map non-unique on the `S`-scheme `E`-torsor it generates, so the `∃!` of
    `universal` fails.  At `N ≤ 2` the automorphism `-1` fixes every point of
    order dividing `2`.
    
    `hcharN` is what makes `N` invertible, hence what makes `PointOfExactOrder`
    agree with Katz–Mazur's `Incl_{Z/N}` and `[Γ₁(N)]` etale rather than merely
    finite flat over `(Ell)`.
